title: BISD Software and Experimental Results for Strict Surface-Unseen Thai Named Entity Recognition
abstract: BISD research software and experimental evidence for strict surface-unseen Thai named entity recognition. The release contains code, configurations, checkpoints and saved predictions for four scratch-model variants across ten paired seeds, together with fixed-gate calibration controls and reproduction instructions. No pretrained encoder is used. Current runs use validation for checkpoint selection and gate calibration; earlier development-stage Test inspection makes the reported comparisons retrospective rather than independent confirmation. Corpus text and gold labels are excluded. Full numerical reproduction requires the exact prepared data specified in README.txt. Extract the code/results ZIP, the full-BISD checkpoint ZIP and all individual checkpoint ZIPs into one directory, preserving internal paths. RELEASE_NOTES.txt explains the archive layout and the CC BY 4.0 license selected for this release.

title: Robust high-fidelity three-qubit gates design for superconducting quantum computers via model-free reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract Multi-qubit gates are crucial to realizing quantum algorithms. Direct implementation of these gates will facilitate a reduction in circuit depth. However, existing model-based methods rely on precise characterization of the system Hamiltonian as well as execution of the control fields, which present challenges in obtaining high fidelity multi-qubit gates. In this paper, we exploit the bang-bang control protocol and model-free reinforcement learning to realize several kinds of three-qubit gates for superconducting quantum computers with tunable/fixed frequency qubits, including the iToffoli gate, the parity check gate and the CCZ gate. The simulation results show that the fidelity of each gate can achieve 99.2% with the Adam Gradient Descent Optimizer. Moreover, the proposed method is robust against random noise in the control pulse. Gate fidelity can be maintained over 95% even in the case of Gaussian noise with variance of 0.3. Besides, the impacts of parameter iterative optimization strategies are also analyzed.

title: Entrepreneurial theorizing with generative artificial intelligence
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Whether large language model (LLM) assistance changes how entrepreneurs construct theories remains unclear. On the one hand, LLMs may help entrepreneurs build more developed causal structures and surface diverse information that supports the formulation of distinctive theories. On the other hand, LLMs may steer causal structures toward conventional forms and discourage the counterintuitive reasoning needed to develop distinctive theories. In a within‐subject experiment with 199 participants theorizing both with and without LLM assistance, we find no significant average treatment effect on either structural or content properties. However, this null average effect masks a redistribution effect, where LLM assistance supplemented theorizing when unaided theories were less developed or distinctive but displaced participants' own theorizing when their theories were already more developed or distinctive. Managerial Summary Large language models (LLMs) can help entrepreneurs develop business ideas by surfacing knowledge across domains and sharpening causal logic. At the same time, LLMs may also push reasoning toward conventional patterns and away from the counterintuitive ideas that are a source of breakthrough opportunities. In a study of 199 participants theorizing with and without LLM assistance, we find that LLMs supported the development of causal structure and content distinctiveness when unaided theories were less developed or distinctive, whereas they had the opposite effect when those theories were already more developed or distinctive. This suggests that while LLMs can scaffold entrepreneurs still developing their theories, greater caution is warranted for those whose theories are already more developed or distinctive, as assistance may diminish those properties.

title: EigDiff: Eigensample Diffusion - or how to significantly reduce training dataset size with marginal performance variation?
abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Current approaches focus on distilling the number of diffusion steps, neglecting potential redundancies of the training data. In this paper, we explore the potential of harnessing eigensamples to train diffusion models on significantly smaller datasets, while preserving model performance. To mitigate the sensitivity to affine transformations of eigenimages, we harness the latent space of a pre-trained CLIP model. We next compute latent eigenvectors by performing principal component analysis (PCA) in CLIP space. Further, we employ eigenvectors as reference points to guide the selection of a representative training set comprising comprising both exemplars (images whose embeddings are closest to eigenvectors) and diverse images. Our comprehensive experiments with different diffusion models applied on multiple datasets indicate that our approach (EigDiff) can reduce training data by up to 14x and accelerate subset selection by up to 1607x, with marginal performance differences.

title: Efficient contextual partial monitoring with general function approximation
abstract: We study finite stochastic partial monitoring (PM) games with side information, a paradigm of sequential learning with partial feedback. On each round $t \in [T]$, both player and environment observe a context and player chooses an action and environment simultaneously chooses an outcome. The player neither observes the outcome nor the loss; instead, they only observe a feedback symbol which is partially informative about the outcome. We utilize the Estimation-to-Decisions (E2D) meta-algorithm of Foster et al.(2021) to design E2D.PMSide, a computationally efficient framework for contextual partial monitoring, which uses an online regression oracle to efficiently estimate the outcome distributions based on historical (context, action, feedback symbol) tuples. title: An NLP pipeline, taxonomy, and models for analysing NHS dental patient feedback (DELIVER Work Stream 2)
abstract: This item contains the research outputs of Work Stream 2 of the EU Horizon DELIVER project, which developed a natural language processing (NLP) pipeline and a clinician-facing dashboard for analysing unstructured patient feedback on NHS dental practices in England.Between June 2019 and April 2024, 57,794 publicly available patient reviews were collected (48,917 after pre-processing). Topic modelling with BERTopic identified 191 topics, which were consolidated into a ten-theme taxonomy through a hybrid approach combining automated first-pass assignment with iterative expert review. The taxonomy informed two fine-tuned DeBERTa models: a four-class sentiment classifier and a multi-label theme classifier. Both models are served behind an interactive dashboard that retrieves and analyses public reviews for a selected dental practice in near real time.The deposit is organised into five parts: the training and modelling scripts with pinned dependencies; the derived taxonomy (topic identifiers, document counts, c-TF-IDF keywords, theme names, and definitions); model cards documenting the two classifiers; deployment documentation for the two inference services; and a versioned snapshot of the dashboard front end. A README indexes the contents, and a data note explains how to assemble a comparable dataset.The raw review text is not included. The reviews can contain personal identifiers, the source NHS Ratings and Reviews API has been retired, and individual reviews are removed at source after two years, so the corpus cannot be redistributed or reconstructed. Only derived, de-identified taxonomy files are shared.

title: Сопоставительное исследование дискурсивных формул в русском и итальянском языках с применением мультимедийных корпусов
abstract: This article examines Russian and Italian discourse formulas using data from multimedia corpora. The study aims to identify the pragmatic and semantic functions of devalorization formulas in Russian and their Italian counterparts. The analysis is conducted within the framework of Construction Grammar and is based on the Pragmaticon, MURCO, Forlixt 3.0, and OPUS corpora. Particular attention is paid to polysemy, pragmatic variation, and the role of context.

title: Convergence bounds for fixed, adaptive, and stochastic gradient methods under Polyak–Łojasiewicz geometry
abstract: The Polyak–Łojasiewicz (PL) inequality offers a useful way to study gradient-based optimization beyond the setting of strong convexity, while still allowing linear convergence under suitable smoothness conditions. This study develops a unified descent-based analysis for fixed-step gradient descent, safeguarded objective-gap step rules, Armijo backtracking, and mini-batch stochastic gradient descent. For the deterministic methods, the analysis provides explicit contraction bounds that show how convergence depends on smoothness, gradient domination, and step-selection parameters. In the stochastic setting, conditional unbiasedness together with a bounded conditional variance leads to a finite-time expectation bound and an upper estimate for the asymptotic residual neighborhood. The analysis is further extended to generalized gradient inequalities. Smooth explicit gradient descent yields linear or polynomial convergence depending on the exponent, whereas superlinear behavior for exponents below one half is established separately for an implicit decrease sequence. This distinction avoids transferring continuous-time behavior directly to explicit discrete gradient iterations. For continuously differentiable squared-error models, uniform spectral bounds on the Jacobian Gram matrix are used to derive regional gradient domination relative to the zero-loss target. A complementary path-length argument gives a sufficient condition for trajectory containment and establishes convergence to zero loss under the stated regional assumptions. Numerical illustrations based on quadratic objectives, power functions, implicit recurrences, stochastic models, and a constant-kernel least-squares example are used to examine the theoretical bounds, accepted Armijo steps, backtracking costs, convergence regimes, and stochastic uncertainty.

title: Halve-Then-Greedy: Adaptive Sampling for Posterior Success with Near-Optimal Instance Dependence
abstract: We study fixed-budget adaptive experimentation aimed at maximizing the probability of obtaining sufficient posterior evidence that a recommended design's mean performance exceeds a target. Unlike best-arm identification, this objective does not require finding the best design. For Gaussian bandits with a Gaussian prior, we propose \emph{Halve-Then-Greedy} (HTG), which combines a large initial balanced allocation, successive halving, and posterior-greedy sampling. We prove instance-dependent, finite-budget exponential bounds on posterior-failure probability that capture both separation from unfavorable arms and the presence of multiple favorable arms. On one-positive-arm families, we establish an asymptotic sample-complexity lower bound that HTG matches up to a logarithmic factor. We further analyze uniform sampling and sequential halving, revealing regimes where they require more samples than HTG by linear and logarithmic factors, respectively. Simulations illustrate HTG's sample-efficiency advantages and their dependence on instance structure.

title: Representation Conditioning for Generation
abstract: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON

title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
abstract: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.

title: JockeyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Horse-Racing Decision-Making
abstract: Repeated event forecasting requires extracting predictive signals from noisy evidence and evaluating their value across successive decisions. We introduce JockeyBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that studies this problem through historical Japanese horse racing. The protocol combines time-gated evidence, priced tools, paired frozen-program controls, and two workflows: executing an LLM-written predictor or acquiring evidence for a fresh per-race LLM forecast. Evaluation separates forecast quality, benchmark-specific net utility, and retrospective betting returns and risk under fixed decision rules. Across 28 model--scaffold configurations on 324 races, paired tests identify seven revision gains and two declines after multiple-testing correction. Yet every configuration has negative mean profit under capped-Kelly settlement. In a four-model comparison, the reusable-program workflow has higher mean betting profit and lower research fees, although both workflows lose on average. Further diagnostics reveal that mean probability bias reverses on selected bets and that profitable individual runs can depend on concentrated returns. These findings motivate evaluating predictive competence, adaptation, resource use, and decision value separately when assessing agents for repeated event forecasting.

title: Secure Enterprise Deployment of Generative AI through LLMOps Governance and Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure
abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) across enterprise environments has created new opportunities forautomation, knowledge management, intelligent decision-making, and customer service. However, deploying large languagemodels (LLMs) in enterprise settings introduces security, privacy, governance, and operational challenges associated with sensitivedata exposure, unauthorized model access, prompt injection, model supply-chain vulnerabilities, and inconsistent regulatorycompliance. Hybrid cloud infrastructure offers a flexible deployment architecture that combines private infrastructure withpublic cloud services, enabling organizations to balance scalability, data sovereignty, and computational efficiency. This researchinvestigates a secure enterprise deployment framework for generative AI by integrating LLMOps governance with hybrid cloudinfrastructure. The proposed framework incorporates model lifecycle management, identity and access controls, data protection,continuous monitoring, model evaluation, and policy-based deployment approval. Security mechanisms include retrieval accessrestrictions, prompt and output validation, encrypted communication, audit logging, and risk-based model selection. Theresearch methodology employs a controlled experimental environment to compare conventional LLM deployment practiceswith the proposed governance-oriented architecture. Evaluation metrics include security incident detection, unauthorized dataexposure, response quality, inference latency, compliance coverage, and operational overhead. The study establishes a systematicfoundation for assessing how integrated LLMOps governance and hybrid cloud controls can improve enterprise AI security whilemaintaining performance, scalability, and operational reliability across diverse organizational environments.

title: A Hybrid Framework Combining Stylometric, Semantic, and SBERT Features for AI-Generated Text Detection
abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has greatly improved the ability of artificial intelligence systems to generate human-like text, making AI-generated text detection more challenging. This study introduces a hybrid framework that merges stylometric and semantic features with Sentence-BERT (SBERT) embeddings to enhance classification performance and robustness. For evaluation, experiments used the AI vs Human Text Dataset. Documents under 50 words were excluded to ensure data quality. The final dataset was balanced, with 100,000 documents evenly split between AI-generated and human-written texts. Stylometric features captured writing style, while semantic features measured sentiment, readability, information density, and lexical. SBERT embeddings captured deep contextual semantics. To improve computational efficiency, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) at 95% variance preservation reduced dimensionality. Four machine learning algorithms—Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and LightGBM—were tested with 10-fold cross-validation. The hybrid framework combined with XGBoost performed best, achieving 98.63% accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.9863, and an ROC-AUC of 0.9987. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test confirmed that the approach significantly outperformed stylometric, semantic, and SBERT-only representations (p-value = 0.0020). Findings show that combining stylometric, semantic, and contextual embedding features captures both surface-level patterns and deep semantics, providing a reliable solution for detecting AI-generated text.

title: D₃ as Minimal Non-Abelian Group for Quantum Ternary Choice on Tianyan-287 — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Dihedral group D₃ (symmetry group of equilateral triangle) is the minimal non-abelian group, directly relevant to modeling non-commutative ternary choice operators in quantum cognition; the Tianyan-287 quantum processor (105 qubits) provides a physical platform for testing such non-abelian group actions in superposition. | MATH: D₃ has order 6, presentation ⟨r, s | r³ = s² = e, srs = r⁻¹⟩. Non-commutativity: sr ≠ rs. Irreducible representations: two 1D (trivial, sign) and one 2D (faithful, with rotation matrix R(2π/3) = [[-1/2, -√3/2], [√3/2, -1/2]] and reflection S = [[1, 0], [0, -1]]). The 2D irrep's character values: χ(e)=2, χ(r)=−1, χ(s)=0. Ternary choice operators in quantum cognition can be represented as elements of D₃ acting on a 3-dimensional Hilbert space basis {|A⟩, |B⟩, |C⟩}, where r cyclically permutes (A→B→C→A) and s swaps two options while fixing the third. | CONNECTION: The 2D irrep of D₃ contains the golden ratio implicitly: eigenvalues of R(2π/3) are e^{±2πi/ Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. title: Two Methodological Pitfalls in Matched-Parameter Quantum–Classical Benchmarking for Paraphrase Identification: Class-Imbalance Collapse and Readout-Offset Asymmetry
abstract: Quantum machine learning is commonly benchmarked by matching a quantum head’s parameter count to that of a classical baseline. We show that this control is insufficient. We compare a 32-parameter parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) head against a nominally matched 31-parameter multi-layer perceptron (MLP) on three paraphrase tasks—the Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus (MRPC), Paraphrase Adversaries from Word Scrambling (PAWS), and Quora Question Pairs (QQP)—and document two pitfalls that inflate an apparent quantum deficit. First, under the tested protocol, unweighted binary cross-entropy on imbalanced data leads to near-all-positive prediction, producing an illusory equivalence. Second, the surviving gap traces to a readout that sits offset from the decision threshold at initialization (⟨Z0⟩=+0.922), and no circuit parameter acts as a threshold shift that could recenter it. A pre-specified calibration experiment removes 61% to 76% of the gap, and a training-free probe detects the condition in one forward pass. Threshold-free metrics then changed our own conclusions. On PAWS, both heads rank barely above chance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, at most 0.508), so the difference there is threshold placement. Only QQP retains a residual, and a post hoc control doubling the qubit count narrows it by 42% without removing it (paired p=0.0009). This pattern is consistent with a capacity or optimization limitation, but does not distinguish between them. Four of five pre-specified predictions failed. Parameter roles and readout offsets must be audited, not only counts.

title: Probabilistic computing with an excitable two-section Q-switched laser
abstract: Probabilistic computing using an excitable two section laser is presented. Excitability, refractory periods, and leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics are all demonstrated, thus proving the device’s functionality as a typical photonic neuron. The laser is perturbed in two distinct ways: first, through electrical perturbations applied to the gain section, and second, through perturbations to the saturable absorber section. Perturbing the saturable absorber section yields clear improvements in delay time and refractory period, thus improving overall operation speed and efficiency. Furthermore, the stochastic nature of the excitability is harnessed to outline the device’s operation as a probabilistic photonic spiking neuron. In particular, the laser is utilised for random-number generation and is demonstrated to satisfy all statistical tests following a single post-processing step.

title: Towards Efficient Threat Intelligence Instruction Tuning via Quality-Aware and Optimal Transport-Guided Data Selection
abstract: High-quality data is essential for improving instruction tuning in threat intelligence analysis. However, existing methods for generating cybersecurity instruction data lack reliable quality assessment mechanisms, and gradient influence-based data selection methods primarily focus on single-sample matching, failing to cover diverse and complex security capabilities. To address these issues, we propose CTI-TDS, a Targeted Data Selection method for instruction tuning in Cyber Threat Intelligence analysis. Specifically, we first filter high-quality CTI instructions by integrating instruction style consistency and security knowledge verification. Furthermore, we formulate gradient influence as a distribution alignment problem, learning a gradient subspace of target tasks and applying entropic regularized optimal transport to optimize distribution matching between training samples and target tasks, enabling diversity-aware data selection. We conduct extensive experiments on CTIBench across multiple large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that when fine-tuning with only a small set of high-value instruction data, CTI-TDS outperforms existing data selection methods and achieves competitive performance on threat intelligence analysis tasks.

title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Wrist cameras provide close-up detail but restrict the view to the end-effector's surroundings. External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

title: Asymptotically Exact Negative Guidance of Diffusion Models via Positive-Unlabeled Learning
abstract: Negative guidance of diffusion models generates samples that avoid an undesired condition, specified either by reference samples or by a conditional score alongside an unconditional model. Existing methods inject repulsive terms derived from local information at each sample, so the resulting sampler does not target an explicit density, and its bias cannot be systematically reduced by increasing computation. We instead present a negative-guidance method that samples from an explicit target density, which uniformly handles both reference-sample and score-based specifications and suppresses probability mass near the undesired condition with an avoidance strength that parametrizes the target density itself. Realizing this target requires estimating, at each diffusion timestep, how likely each sample is to belong to the undesired condition. We cast this estimation as a Positive-Unlabeled learning problem that admits lightweight online training along the diffusion trajectory, using condition samples as positives and diffusion particles as unlabeled data. Because the guided particles drift from the unconditional marginal, we further correct the residual mismatch via Sequential Monte Carlo, yielding a sampler that is asymptotically exact in the particle limit and that turns any existing negative-guidance method into its proposal kernel. Empirically, our method approaches the ground-truth target on Gaussian mixtures and Pareto-dominates existing methods on trade-offs between avoidance and generation quality, distributional bias, and diversity, including in an image-generation setting with a pretrained score network.

title: Projected Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Flows for Hawkes Background-Intensity Estimation
abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the background intensity of a Hawkes process when the triggering mechanism is known, treating the background as an unknown finite positive measure with a regular density. We propose a likelihood-based variational approach based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry. In this setting, the relevant first variations are naturally distribution-valued and therefore fall outside the classical gradient-flow formulation. We develop a distributional framework for the resulting dynamics and give them a finite-dimensional meaning through projections onto statistical manifolds. We identify the true background as the unique zero of a limiting generalized gradient and, under suitable stability, compactness, integrability and approximation conditions, establish a conditional consistency theorem for measurable estimators satisfying the empirical projected equations on events whose probabilities tend to one. Finally, we specialize the construction to Gaussian-mixture manifolds and obtain an explicit finite-dimensional scheme.

title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
abstract: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. Three research questions ask: (1) how leaders describe adoption trajectories, maturity, and organizational arrangements; (2) how they reconcile regulation with creative, operational, and governance innovation; and (3) how they frame workforce roles, emerging competencies, and human oversight. Technology–organization–environment, diffusion-of-innovation, and organizational sensemaking perspectives inform interpretation. Nine themes were developed: production-grade diffusion; regulation as creative discipline; industrialized versus distinctive content; personalization and data trust; practitioner-led implementation; divergent workforce responses; critical-thinking demands; human-in-the-loop brand safety; and a shift toward generative engine optimization. Timestamped excerpts and explicit code-to-theme and theme-to-question mappings substantiate the analysis. These findings describe public executive narratives, not independently verified organizational outcomes. A single public transcript and single-analyst interpretation limit transferability and preclude statistical generalization. The principal contribution is a transparent, theory-informed example of analyzing public executive discourse and a foundation for subsequent multi-source research.

title: QisDebug: Zero-Touch Instrumentation and Timeline Debugging for Qiskit
abstract: QisDebug attaches construction, transpilation and execution tracing to existing Qiskit code with a single start() call, records everything that happens to each circuit on one timeline (including mid-execution statevectors on Aer), and explores that timeline in a native GUI, a terminal viewer, or through an MCP server for coding agents.

title: Interaction Bindings and Local Policies in Distributed Boolean Coordination
abstract: This preprint examines whether inherited interaction arrangements can acquire and transfer useful collective computation while local operations remain fixed. A fully inspectable four-agent Boolean model separates structural opportunity, learned organisation and transferable function. A separately specified 100-world replication finds a developed-minus-initial reserved-case accuracy gain of 0.2584, with a 95% confidence interval of [0.2034, 0.3135], meeting the internally fixed 0.10 lower-bound criterion. All worlds are retained, including 21 negative gains. All 200 replication trajectories were replayed, and the primary calculation was independently recomputed from saved programs. Prespecification was internal, rather than external preregistration; secondary contrasts remain descriptive. Supporting exploratory studies include crossed inheritance, compatible transfer, event-order disruption and restoration, structural feasibility analysis and a five-task comparator. A supplied viable arrangement allows local-policy search to outperform binding search in the related task family. A formal appendix demonstrates why access to every input does not necessarily provide sufficient intermediate memory: exhaustive enumeration of 4,096 relevant local-table assignments verifies the bottleneck example. The results support bounded acquisition and causal function under supplied interfaces. They do not establish intrinsic superiority of external storage, a new evolutionary individual or descendant reconstruction. The self-only comparator does not match the number of distinct candidate proposals, and the tasks remain within a pair-composition family. Broader task and search comparisons are identified as future work. Close genetic-programming and distributed-program precedents are acknowledged. The accompanying reproducibility package contains executable code, raw states and decision traces, protocols, source hashes, world-level analyses, independent implementation checks, deterministic diagnostic data, and preserved development versions and negative results.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Verification and Cross-Agent Verification in Multi-Agent Systems: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Verification Coordination
abstract: Verification is a fundamental requirement for reliable multi-agent systems. An agent may evaluate its own reasoning, intermediate states, decisions, and outputs, while other agents may independently inspect, challenge, reproduce, or validate the same results. However, relying exclusively on self-verification can preserve internal blind spots, whereas continuously invoking cross-agent verification can increase computational costs, communication overhead, and coordination complexity. Moreover, neither strategy is universally optimal across all tasks, agents, environmental conditions, or stages of problem solving. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching Between Self-Verification and Cross-Agent Verification (ASSCV), a general framework that dynamically selects verification strategies according to estimated uncertainty, task risk, historical verification performance, inter-agent disagreement, evidence independence, and verification cost. The framework supports self-verification, cross-agent verification, sequential verification, parallel verification, and selective escalation between these modes. Unlike a fixed verification pipeline, ASSCV treats the choice of verification strategy as a state-dependent decision that can be revised throughout task execution. The framework is applicable to heterogeneous and homogeneous multi-agent systems, including but not limited to artificial intelligence agents, autonomous software agents, robotic agents, distributed decision-making systems, and collaborative reasoning systems. The paper formalizes the verification state, switching policy, expected verification utility, agent reliability memory, and termination conditions. It also presents a reference algorithm, a theoretical analysis of verification selection under explicit assumptions, and a reproducible experimental protocol for evaluating accuracy, error detection, calibration, computational cost, communication overhead, and robustness. No empirical superiority is assumed in advance. The principal research proposition is that adaptive coordination between individual and collective verification may offer a more efficient reliability-control strategy than permanently using either mode alone. The proposed framework provides a testable foundation for investigating when, why, and how multi-agent systems should switch between self-verification and cross-agent verification.

title: ARWLF: source code, git history and evidence for "Adaptive Wide-Leaf Filtering for Exact Ternary Representation Root Reporting"
abstract: Source code, complete git history and evidence for the article "Adaptive Wide-Leaf Filtering for Exact Ternary Representation Root Reporting" (Naman Menasagi), submitted to ACM Transactions on Algorithms. ARWLF (Adaptive Radix Wide-Leaf Filter) is an exact root reporter for the final ternary merge of a Ternary Representation Technique (TER) algorithm for random Subset Sum. It routes each source pair to a unique target leaf with explicit carry and rejects pairs with byte-occupancy filters before any candidate is recovered. On authentic dimension-108 roots, a single-core AVX2 implementation is a geometric-mean 53.1 times faster than the frozen tile-sweep baseline on calibration microproblems. On a complete prepared root of 25 trillion logical pairs it takes 57–60 minutes against 54.8 hours, with identical output. Files: - subset-sum-ter-fft-6d8e21d-source.zip: the repository at commit 6d8e21d(C++20 sources, frozen backends, campaign harnesses, raw results, the paper and its build scripts). - subset-sum-ter-fft-6d8e21d.bundle: the complete git history. Clone it with git clone subset-sum-ter-fft-6d8e21d.bundle -b main. The history is needed to recover the exact sources of the experiment builds, which were made from trees with uncommitted changes. - SHA256SUMS.txt: SHA-256 hashes of both files. To verify, start with reviewer/README.md in a clone of the bundle: - python reviewer/check_build_sources.py recovers the campaign-build sources; - reviewer/check_integrity.ps1 checks the frozen sources and the recorded inputs; - reviewer/check_paper.ps1 regenerates every table and figure and checks them against the article. The 0.84–1.03 GB dimension-108 root snapshots are not included; they are regenerated deterministically from their recorded seeds.

title: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself
abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Motivated by this finding, we believe the devil of spatial reasoning lies in 3D itself, and introduce DeSpatial(Devil of Spatial), which explicitly decomposes spatial understanding into perception and reasoning. DeSpatial has a shared 3D perception tool to reconcile independent perception outputs into a unified, metric, gravity-aligned 3D scene. This perception tool has two core components: a) a joint segmentation--depth co-refinement module that consolidates masks of the same object and removes projection artifacts caused by inconsistent segmentation and depth within a single frame; b) a cross-view instance fusion module that consolidate voxel-overlapping instances but not allowed to merge same-frame instances. This fusion module additionally fuses spatially disjoint fragments caused by insufficient multi-view observations, by checking their 3D structure and source mask appearance. After receiving the complete and unified 3D scene information, the agent chooses reasoning or computational tools to solve the spatial problem. DeSpatial achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video results on VSI-SUPER, revealing the bottleneck of spatial understanding lies in a precise 3D perception itself.

title: Ekologi Media Linguistik Non-Kekerasan: Negosiasi Empati dan Keamanan dalam Komunikasi Manusia-AI
abstract: Kecerdasan buatan generatif semakin menjadi mediator dalam komunikasi antarmanusia, menim bulkan pertanyaan mendasar tentang bagaimana teknologi ini mengelola makna, emosi, dan keamanan psikologis dalam ruang digital. Penelitian ini mengkaji ekologi media linguistik non-kekerasan yang muncul dari negosiasi empati dan keamanan dalam komunikasi manusia-AI. Menggunakan kerangka Coordinated Management of Meaning (CMM), yang mengidentifikasi tiga dimensi penting dalam dialog berkelanjutan koherensi (pemahaman bersama), koordinasi (penyelarasan tindakan), dan misteri (pengakuan atas apa yang tidak dapat sepenuhnya dijelaskan) penelitian ini mengeksplorasi bagaimana agen AI dapat berfungsi sebagai mediator dalam percakapan yang terfragmentasi secara emosional dan berpotensi konfliktual . Pendekatan penelitian menggunakan studi kasus eksperimental pada dialog dengan topik sensitif secara politik dan budaya, dengan melibatkan agen AI yang dirancang berdasarkan prinsip CMM . Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa agen AI generatif dapat mengurangi hambatan emosional dan memfasilitasi dialog yang lebih hormat dan inklusif, terutama bagi pengguna yang tidak terbiasa dengan diskusi semacam itu. Dengan menyempurnakan pernyataan pengguna secara strategis dan memodulasi nada berdasarkan gaya resolusi konflik, agen ini dapat mempromosikan pengakuan timbal balik dan meningkatkan kualitas wacana . Namun, temuan juga menyoroti keterbatasan: penerapan strategi yang terlalu kaku atau penghalusan emosi yang berlebihan dapat mengurangi keaslian pembicara atau menghambat ekspresi kritis. Penelitian ini juga mengungkap bahwa dalam konteks multibahasa, AI mengungkap dan menyembunyikan aspek makna budaya yang disebut sebagai "misteri" ketika berhadapan dengan topik-topik sensitif secara sosial. Ketika AI menerjemahkan atau memformat ulang pesan antar bahasa, terjadi negosiasi antara kejelasan dan ambiguitas, antara kenyamanan emosional dan akurasi faktual . Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa ekologi media linguistik non-kekerasan memerlukan keseimbangan yang hati-hati antara kenyamanan emosional, agensi ekspresif, dan adaptasi yang peka terhadap konteks dalam desain sistem AI komunikatif. Implikasi temuan ini penting bagi pengembang AI, pembuat kebijakan, dan praktisi komunikasi dalam merancang sistem yang mendukung dialog yang aman dan empatik tanpa mengorbankan kebebasan berekspresi dan pemikiran kritis. Ekologi media yang berkelanjutan menuntut AI yang tidak hanya efisien, tetapi juga peka terhadap kompleksitas komunikasi manusia.

Penelitian ini mengkaji ekologi media linguistik non-kekerasan yang muncul dari negosiasi empati dan keamanan dalam komunikasi manusia-AI. Menggunakan kerangka Coordinated Management of Meaning (CMM), yang mengidentifikasi tiga dimensi penting dalam dialog berkelanjutan koherensi (pemahaman bersama), koordinasi (penyelarasan tindakan), dan misteri (pengakuan atas apa yang tidak dapat sepenuhnya dijelaskan) penelitian ini mengeksplorasi bagaimana agen AI dapat berfungsi sebagai mediator dalam percakapan yang terfragmentasi secara emosional dan berpotensi konfliktual . Pendekatan penelitian menggunakan studi kasus eksperimental pada dialog dengan topik sensitif secara politik dan budaya, dengan melibatkan agen AI yang dirancang berdasarkan prinsip CMM . Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa agen AI generatif dapat mengurangi hambatan emosional dan memfasilitasi dialog yang lebih hormat dan inklusif, terutama bagi pengguna yang tidak terbiasa dengan diskusi semacam itu. Dengan menyempurnakan pernyataan pengguna secara strategis dan memodulasi nada berdasarkan gaya resolusi konflik, agen ini dapat mempromosikan pengakuan timbal balik dan meningkatkan kualitas wacana . Namun, temuan juga menyoroti keterbatasan: penerapan strategi yang terlalu kaku atau penghalusan emosi yang berlebihan dapat mengurangi keaslian pembicara atau menghambat ekspresi kritis. Penelitian ini juga mengungkap bahwa dalam konteks multibahasa, AI mengungkap dan menyembunyikan aspek makna budaya yang disebut sebagai "misteri" ketika berhadapan dengan topik-topik sensitif secara sosial. Ketika AI menerjemahkan atau memformat ulang pesan antar bahasa, terjadi negosiasi antara kejelasan dan ambiguitas, antara kenyamanan emosional dan akurasi faktual . Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa ekologi media linguistik non-kekerasan memerlukan keseimbangan yang hati-hati antara kenyamanan emosional, agensi ekspresif, dan adaptasi yang peka terhadap konteks dalam desain sistem AI komunikatif. Implikasi temuan ini penting bagi pengembang AI, pembuat kebijakan, dan praktisi komunikasi dalam merancang sistem yang mendukung dialog yang aman dan empatik tanpa mengorbankan kebebasan berekspresi dan pemikiran kritis. Ekologi media yang berkelanjutan menuntut AI yang tidak hanya efisien, tetapi juga peka terhadap kompleksitas komunikasi manusia.
evidence.venue: MUARA BAHASA : Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Bahasa & Komunikasi

title: CAT'S Theory: The Meta-Ontological Invariant: Pre-Axiomatic Priority, Triadic Modal Completeness, and Shannon Channel Equivalence
abstract: CAT'S Theory — Foundational Layer-1 Anchor Manuscript: Every formal system presupposes structural conditions under which its axioms function as axioms and its invariants function as invariants, yet no axiom-dependent framework derives these conditions from within itself. Within CAT'S Theory, we demonstrate that these preconditions are governed by a single multiplicative meta-ontological invariant, R = Ψ × I × Pr ≠ 0 (Pattern × Intent × Presence), established from zero axioms by two-stage retorsion. First, we prove that any functioning axiom or invariant requires determinate structure (Ψ > 0), directed state-space narrowing (I > 0), and operative instantiation (Pr > 0), and that any attempt to deny the invariant performatively instantiates all three factors. Second, we prove that Claude Shannon's three-component communication channel (X, p(y|x), Y) is structurally isomorphic to the triadic invariant (I, Ψ, Pr), with channel capacity C > 0 ⟺ R ≠ 0. Third, we formalize the triadic modal logic Ψ–ℐ–Π, prove via an explicit Kripke bisimulation that standard two-axis modal logic (□, ◊) is formally blind to state-space narrowing (conflating genuine necessities with unnarrowed Shells), and establish soundness and canonical-model completeness for the triadic axiom system. Fourth, we establish the 2 × 3 × 2 (12-cell) decomposition of Intent, prove the Co-Necessity Theorem (I_α > 0 ⟺ I_ω > 0) and Gap Elimination at the self-grounding fixed point R = Φ(R), and derive the Landauer thermodynamic floor E_min = μ(w) k_B T ln 2 per narrowing event. Finally, we prove the Axiom-Channel Equivalence Theorem—showing that frontier mathematical programs (Grothendieck's motives, Joyal's simplex category, Homotopy Type Theory, Voevodsky's triangulated motives, and ZFC set theory) operate as capacity-limited Shannon encodings of R—and unify Gödel's incompleteness theorem, Shannon's capacity bound, and the Ouroboros fixed-point condition into a single Self-Reference Bound.

title: Robust Prediction-Reliability Assessment in Biomedical Sensing and Classification Under Data Scarcity Using Conformal Prediction and Statistical Randomization
abstract: Reliable assessment of prediction reliability is important in biomedical sensing and measurement applications, where machine learning models increasingly transform imaging, physiological, chemical, and molecular measurements into clinically relevant predictions. Such applications often operate under limited labeled data because sensor acquisition, experimental measurement, and expert annotation can be costly, while biological and measurement variability can further challenge model development. Under these conditions, reliability scores derived from standard inductive conformal prediction (ICP) can be sensitive to the particular division of available data into proper-training and calibration subsets. To address this issue, we propose three randomized ICP variants: bootstrapping ICP (BICP), randomized ICP (RICP), and out-of-bag ICP (OOB-ICP), to improve the informativeness and repeated-sampling stability of conformal-derived prediction-reliability scores under data scarcity. We benchmarked these methods using a controlled simulation and three real-world biomedical sensing and measurement applications: pneumonia diagnosis from X-ray radiography, alternative herbal medicine classification using a 16-channel semiconductor electronic-nose gas-sensing system, and breast cancer subtyping from RNA-seq molecular measurements. Results show that the proposed methods produce aggregate credibility scores that are informative of prediction correctness and less sensitive to randomness in training-data sampling. Empirical prediction-set coverage analyses further characterize the behavior of the aggregated conformity scores relative to nominal error levels without assuming that they retain the exact finite-sample validity of conventional conformal p-values. Among the evaluated methods, OOB-ICP achieved strong overall classification performance and informative, stable prediction-reliability scores, supporting statistical randomization as a practical strategy for stabilizing conformal-derived reliability assessment under limited training data in biomedical sensing and measurement applications.

title: Anticipated Acceptance of AI-Proactive Smart Sofas: A Value–Reactance Dual-Pathway Model
abstract: Proactive AI can make domestic products more responsive while raising concerns about unwanted intervention, control, and privacy. This study examines anticipated acceptance of AI-proactive smart sofas through a value–reactance framework. A theory-guided exploratory sequential mixed-methods design combinedinterviews with 10 prospective users and a scenario-based survey of 401 valid cases. PLS-SEM showed that perceived AI proactivity was positively associated with perceived usefulness and perceived intrusiveness, although the usefulness-related coefficient was substantially larger. Perceived usefulness was positively associated with AI trust and behavioral intention, whereas perceived intrusiveness was positively associated with psychological reactance, which was negatively associated with AI trust and behavioral intention. Privacy sensitivity positively moderated the intrusiveness–reactance association, although the interaction was small. Because participants evaluated a hypothetical product rather than interacting with an actual sofa, behavioral intention is interpreted as anticipated acceptance rather than observed adoption. The findings highlight user control, transparency, and privacy as design considerations.

title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Improving the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) often relies on post-training with supervision from stronger models. Two common strategies are supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which trains on teacher-generated demonstrations, and on-policy distillation (OPD), which provides teacher feedback on trajectories generated by the student itself. While OPD can be more data-efficient by supervising student-generated trajectories, it is unclear how the teacher's supervision at each state affects the student's learned behavior. To study this question, we conduct a controlled comparison of OPD and filtered SFT across data budgets and tasks where the teacher exhibits different levels of reliability, and analyze how these differences shape student accuracy and completion behavior. Across the two tasks, we find that OPD is effective only when the teacher remains reliable on student-generated trajectories. On ChartQA, where the teacher completes 99% of its solutions, OPD trained on only 10% of the data comes within 1.4 accuracy points of full-data SFT. In contrast, on Geometry3K, where the teacher fails to complete 22% of its solutions, OPD underperforms SFT by 7.9 points, with most of the gap explained by incomplete responses. More strikingly, starting OPD from an SFT student reduces its completion rate from 76% to 62%, effectively erasing the completion behavior learned through SFT. Filtering teacher demonstrations for completeness alone recovers much of SFT's advantage. These results show that on-policy supervision can transfer not only teacher knowledge but also persistent failure modes on student-visited states. Code is available at https://github.com/ffy208/opd-inherits-teacher-vlm.

title: The Impact of Detector Architecture, Model Scale, and Scene Density on Multi-Pedestrian Tracking
abstract: Pedestrian tracking in video is important for applications such as surveillance and scene analysis, but it becomes more challenging in crowded scenarios with frequent occlusions and rapid motion. This paper analyzes how detector architecture, model scale, scene density, and inference regime affect the tracking of multiple pedestrians. We compare the YOLO11, RT-DETR, and YOLO26 detector families with the ByteTrack and BoT-SORT trackers on sequences from the MOT17, MOT20, and SOMPT22 benchmarks. For YOLO26, we also compare traditional overlap filtering via Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) with end-to-end inference. The RT-DETR family achieved the highest mean scores on the HOTA tracking quality metric across all three benchmarks with both trackers, with a more pronounced advantage on MOT20, albeit at a higher computational cost. On MOT17 and SOMPT22, YOLO26 variants, especially YOLO26-L with NMS, offered favorable combinations of quality and speed compared with RT-DETR. In the YOLO26 inference comparison, the end-to-end mode did not yield consistent tracking gains over the NMS-based regime. Taken together, these results provide a practical guide for selecting detectors and trackers for this task based on application priorities.

title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
abstract: Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods. Recently, flow matching has emerged as a strong generative paradigm for modeling complex data distributions, with successful applications across diverse domains. These advances motivate us to systematically investigate flow matching for MSS in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo. Specifically, we investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints. Beyond the signal-level metrics commonly used for MSS, such as signal-to-distortion ratio, we further evaluate MSS methods using embedding-based metrics, as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark. On MUSDB18-HQ, our proposed model exhibits competitive performance in both objective and subjective tests, highlighting the potential of flow matching for generative MSS. Demo: https://ik4sumii.github.io/FLOMSS/

title: Visualización de datos con Python
abstract: Este laboratorio es una guía paso a paso para la visualización de datos utilizando Python. A través del uso de bibliotecas como pandas, matplotlib y seaborn, se analiza un conjunto de datos del sector automotriz, explorando relaciones entre variables mediante gráficos como histogramas, diagramas de dispersión, mapas de calor, boxplots y gráficos de barras.

title: Deep learning-based profanity detection in social media: a survey in the context of toxic language detection
abstract: The spread of toxic and profane language across online platforms has necessitated the development of advanced automated detection systems to maintain safe online environments. This survey comprehensively explores the progression of profanity language detection techniques, focusing on datasets, feature extraction methods, and model architectures. Through a thorough examination of key developments in the field, the study outlines the evolution of detection systems across four distinct phases. It offers a taxonomy of approaches that have shaped the current landscape. We review various high-performing models, highlighting their effectiveness in addressing challenges such as context understanding, multilingual data, and identifying subtle forms of toxicity. The article further explores the strengths of these models, including their ability to capture long-range dependencies and nuanced features, while also discussing their limitations, such as computational efficiency and generalization across datasets. By analyzing the current state of toxic language detection and the latest advancements in feature extraction and modeling techniques, we provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners. Additionally, the article outlines future research directions, emphasizing the importance of lightweight, adaptive models and real-time optimization techniques to enable scalable, practical deployment across diverse platforms and environments.

title: Bayesian local clustering of functional data via semi-Markovian random partitions
abstract: We introduce a Bayesian framework for indirect local clustering of functional data, leveraging B-spline basis expansions and a novel dependent random partition model. By exploiting the local support properties of B-splines, our approach allows partially coincident functional behaviors, achieved when shared basis coefficients span sufficiently contiguous regions. This is accomplished through a cutting-edge dependent random partition model that enforces semi-Markovian dependence across a sequence of partitions. By matching the degree of the B-spline basis with the semi-Markovian dependence structure, the proposed model serves as a highly flexible prior, enabling efficient modeling of localized features in functional data. Furthermore, we extend the utility of the dependent random partition model beyond functional data, demonstrating its applicability to a broad class of problems where sequences of dependent partitions are central, and standard Markovian assumptions prove overly restrictive. Empirical illustrations, including analyses of simulated data and tide level measurements from the Venice Lagoon, showcase the effectiveness and versatility of the proposed methodology.

title: Pre-M7 T6 High-Assurance Benchmark: Public Pre-Evaluation Registration and Cryptographic Commitment
authors: Mohamed Mohamed Sabry Abdel Halim Mohamed El-Nashar
abstract: Public pre-evaluation registration for an M7 T6 high-assurance benchmark. The underlying candidate systems are proprietary and remain confidential. This record publishes only non-sensitive benchmark commitments, execution counts, anti-leakage boundaries, and cryptographic hashes that bind the confidential frozen package before M7 execution. No proprietary system architecture, prompts, orchestration logic, internal protocols, implementation details, hidden case contents, or answer keys are disclosed. Future records may report aggregate benchmark results while preserving the confidentiality of the underlying systems.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Rewarding and Mutual-Rewarding in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can evaluate their own generated responses and use the resulting feedback to improve subsequent outputs. However, self-rewarding may reinforce systematic errors, preserve blind spots, and produce unreliable preference signals when a model evaluates content according to the same limitations that affected its generation. Mutual-rewarding, in which multiple LLMs evaluate one another's outputs, provides an alternative source of feedback but introduces additional computational costs, evaluator disagreements, correlated biases, and the possibility of reciprocal error reinforcement. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Rewarding and Mutual-Rewarding (ASSMR), a multi-LLM framework that dynamically selects between self-rewarding and mutual-rewarding according to estimated reward reliability, model disagreement, uncertainty, task difficulty, computational cost, and feedback history. Rather than permanently adopting either an individual evaluation pathway or a cross-model evaluation pathway, ASSMR treats the selection of the reward source as a decision-making problem. Each model can evaluate its own output when its self-evaluation is sufficiently reliable, request evaluations from other models when independent feedback is expected to be more valuable, or combine both mechanisms when neither source is sufficiently reliable on its own. The framework introduces a reward-source switching policy, reliability-aware reward aggregation, a switching-cost mechanism, and an optional learning component for updating the selection policy from subsequent evaluation outcomes. It distinguishes the generation of reward signals from the optimization of model parameters, allowing the framework to operate in both inference-time self-improvement systems and training-time preference optimization pipelines. A controlled experimental protocol is proposed to compare adaptive switching against fixed self-rewarding, fixed mutual-rewarding, and non-adaptive hybrid baselines. The framework is intended to investigate whether adaptive reward-source selection can improve evaluation reliability, downstream task performance, robustness, and computational efficiency. These benefits remain empirical hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

title: The Blume-Capel Model as a $φ^6$ Field Theory: A Monte Carlo and Flow Model Study
abstract: We report Monte Carlo simulations of a continuous spin variant of the Blume-Capel model. We compute the phase diagrams in the crystal-field-temperature plane, as a function of the softness of the spins. We show that normalizing flows, a class of generative models capable of direct sampling without autocorrelation, are effective samplers across the phase diagram, including in the first-order transition region and in the vicinity of the tricritical point. Finite-size scaling analyses of flow samples locate the first- and second-order transitions as well as the tricritical point with accuracy comparable to canonical and extended-ensemble Monte Carlo.

title: The Reach of Treatment Effects: Randomization Inference for Zero-Effect Regions
abstract: A treatment may affect some individuals while leaving others unaffected. We study the reach of treatment effects by asking how large an unaffected covariate region could be. We develop efficient local randomization tests over nearest-neighbour regions to construct a finite-sample valid upper confidence bound for the size of the largest zero-effect region. A small bound provides evidence that treatment effects extend broadly across covariate values by ruling out large zero-effect regions. Under a general outcome model, we characterize how the size of the bound depends on the number of affected units, the size of their treatment effects, and the geometry of the true zero-effect set. We show that, when region size is measured as a sample fraction, the excess of the upper confidence bound over the true size decreases to zero at a minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor. Numerical simulations assess the coverage, power and computational efficiency of our method. Applications to voter-turnout, HIV clinical-trial, and AI-assisted writing data illustrate how our method rules out large zero-effect regions across the covariates of interest.

title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
abstract: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
abstract: In Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning, large language models may correctly infer the agent's mental state but fail to use that inference when predicting or judging the agent's subsequent actions. In this work, we investigate whether explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action with rules improves ToM reasoning. We generate concise \textit{if--then} rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks. GRPO with rule generation outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and think reasoning. Moreover, rules generated by larger models ($\geq$3B) provide transferable knowledge that improves downstream performance of GPT-4o-mini. These findings suggest that explicit rules help models bridge the reasoning gap in ToM and support knowledge transfer across models.

title: CIRCA annotation disagreement and linguistic selection: code and reproducibility materials
abstract: Reproducibility materials for “Label aggregation and the linguistic composition of corpus subsets: Evidence from CIRCA indirect-answer annotations” by Qingling Zhao and Xinyu Guo. The workflow links disagreement at label boundaries, item-level changes under aggregation and majority filtering, and the linguistic material retained by those changes. This repository contains analysis code, fixed extraction rules, aggregate outputs, source checksums and executable checks. Original CIRCA data are obtained separately from the pinned official source. Project-owned code uses the MIT licence; third-party corpus excerpts retain their source notices. No new participant data or corpus annotations are included. Funding: Shandong Provincial Social Science Planning Research Project, Grant No. 24DYYJ03 to Xinyu Guo.

title: Superdense Coding with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes over Lossy Bosonic Channels: Square and Hexagonal Lattices Compared
abstract: We analyze superdense coding with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP)-encoded bosonic modesover a lossy channel of transmissivity η, for square and hexagonal lattices. Combining loss, aquantum-limited pre-amplifier and the finite squeezing of both modes of the shared pair gives a twomode noise variance σ2eff = κ∆2 + (1 − η) for Bob’s destructive Bell measurement, with κ = 2 forindependent per-mode noise. Both lattices are treated in the same periodic model: Bob’s outcomeis a lattice point plus Gaussian noise, and the logical symbol is the class of that point modulo thestabilizer lattice. We report the capacity of the measured channel (mutual information with the rawoutcome) and the rate of hard-decision nearest-lattice-point decoding, the protocol as described.Both are computed by deterministic quadrature and checked against Monte Carlo. The hexagonaladvantage is modest and depends on the operating point. For the capacity, the hexagonal latticetolerates about 0.09 dB more noise variance at 1.5 bits and 0.17 dB more at 90% of the two-bitceiling (1.8 bits), approaching but staying below its 0.625 dB geometric coding gain as the errorrate falls, and it is slightly worse below about 1 bit; for hard decisions the crossover is near 1.4bits. The larger minimum distance is partly offset by six nearest neighbours (four for the squarelattice) and, for hard decisions, by a larger error entropy. For a 1.8-bit capacity the square latticeneeds 8.3, 9.7 and 12.4 dB of squeezing at η = 0.99, 0.95 and 0.90, of which the hexagonal latticesaves 0.19, 0.25 and 0.46 dB. Under thermal loss the saving grows only through the rising noisefloor, for which we give an exact expression. Evaluated at the pre-amplifier GKP resource energyNS (smaller than the energy actually entering the channel, which the pre-amplifier raises), thecapacity of GKP superdense coding stays below both the entanglement-assisted and the unassisted(Holevo) capacities of the channel throughout our sweep, never exceeding 0.65 of the latter in theexplored thermal-loss range. Using NS rather than the larger physical transmitted energy makesthis comparison favourable to GKP, while not charging the retained mode or the cost of distributingthe entangled pair makes it favourable to superdense coding; within this convention we find noadvantage over unassisted classical communication.

title: Sleight: A Language for LLMs
abstract: Slides for a talk on Sleight, a programming language with restricted dependent types whose proofs erase at compile time, designed for LLMs to write, and on an agent runner that tests whether models can write it. In the main task, models write a fast, in-place heapsort certified correct against a supplied specification; 25 of 28 runs across 10 models passed, and their sorts run in about the time of handwritten C and OCaml. The talk also covers what the models found hard, an attempt to have agents prove False, and the language itself: erasure and uniqueness declared on every binder, zero-cost coercions, memory locations tracked separately from values, termination by first-class levels, Type : Type with no positivity check, Kernel-style first-class special forms, and three implementations (an OCaml reference interpreter, a self-hosted compiler, and a Lean 4 model with a machine-checked soundness proof for a fragment). An appendix gives further examples, the soundness sketch, and the full benchmark tables. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23361871

title: M7-R2 T6 High-Assurance Benchmark: Corrected Pre-Evaluation Registration and Cryptographic
authors: Mohamed Mohamed Sabry Abdel Halim Mohamed El-Nashar
abstract: Public pre-evaluation registration for the corrected M7-R2 T6 high-assurance benchmark. M7-R1 was terminated fail-closed before final scoring because required pre-frozen fixture descriptor fields were incomplete. M7-R2 corrects that design deficiency before any new candidate execution. At the time of this registration:- all 36 fixture descriptors were complete;- scoring rules were frozen;- the ground-truth firewall was verified;- M7-R2 execution had not started;- M7-R2 ground truth had not been accessed. The underlying candidate systems remain proprietary and confidential. This record publishes only non-sensitive benchmark commitments and cryptographic provenance. No proprietary system architecture, prompts, orchestration logic, internal protocols, implementation details, hidden case contents, or answer keys are disclosed. Future records may report aggregate benchmark results while preserving the confidentiality of the underlying systems.

title: Bridging the sim-to-real gap in embodied robot learning: methods and experimental studies
abstract: Learning for embodied robots typically relies on simulated environments. However, physical model deviations and dynamic noise create a sim-to-real gap, limiting the deployment of trained policies in the real world. This paper investigates the coupling mechanisms of this gap across dynamics, control, and cognition, and constructs a three-tier progressive methodology of“ dynamics enhancement– control closed‑loop–cognitive reasoning. ”A comparative analysis of mainstream algorithms is conducted in a unified testing environment. Experimental results reveal that single‑dimensional optimization possesses an upper limit in disturbance resistance; control‑layer feedback effectively curbs the accumulation of low‑level physical errors; and cognitive‑layer large models significantly break through the generalization bottleneck in unseen scenarios. Consequently, a multi‑layer collaborative architecture that integrates low‑level error suppression with high‑level semantic cognition emerges as a superior systemic path to bridge the cross‑domain deployment gap.

title: How to Train Your Little Dragon: Teaching a Small Language Model to Construct and Refine GPU Optimization Scripts
abstract: Compiler transformations interact, making GPU kernel optimization a search for combinations that preserve the computation while improving performance. We introduce HOW TO TRAIN YOUR LITTLE DRAGON, a training method that teaches a small language model both to construct complete optimization scripts and to improve existing ones. Instead of ranking candidates or generating kernel code, our model generates optimization scripts. We devise a compact, lossless representation whose deterministic decoding reconstructs the exact compiler trace, preserving its transformation parameters and dependencies. We use a compiler framework TVM MetaSchedule to build training data on 54,116 distinct workloads, and construct 108,594 examples in two training sets: 60,236 teach the model to generate an optimized script from an unoptimized kernel, while 48,358 teach it to produce a better script given the kernel and a somewhat optimized script. Supervised fine-tuning teaches the model to construct and improve optimization scripts from these search-derived examples. We then add reinforcement learning with a shaped reward that combines correctness with measured performance, awarding a latency-based bonus only to numerically correct kernels. We apply this training method to a model with 8 billion parameters. After supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, the model achieves per-attempt correctness of 91.27% for construction and 92.01% for refinement, while reinforcement learning produces faster kernels than supervised training on 88 of 102 construction tasks and 145 of 170 refinement prompts. With only 8B parameters, our LITTLE DRAGON achieves higher per-attempt correctness and better kernel performance than six frontier LLMs: GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3 among them, each with hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters, for which task-specific training is unavailable or expensive.

title: Secret Sharing from Non-Extractable Randomness
abstract: Bosley and Dodis (TCC 2007) proved that a class of imperfect randomness sources that suffices for information-theoretic encryption of messages longer than the logarithm of the key length must admit deterministic extraction of nearly uniform bits, and asked whether the same is true of two-out-of-two secret sharing. Aggarwal, Chung, Obremski, and Ribeiro (TCC 2022) gave a positive answer for schemes that are in addition leakage-resilient or non-malleable; the original question remained open. We answer it in the negative. For every $b\ge2$ we construct a class of flat sources on $\{0,1\}^{b+2}$, each of min-entropy at least $b$, together with a perfectly correct and perfectly private two-out-of-two scheme that shares a $b$-bit secret into two $(b+1)$-bit shares using any source in the class, and we show that every deterministic map from $\{0,1\}^{b+2}$ to $\{0,1\}$ is at statistical distance at least $1/6$ from uniform on some source in the class. This implies that sharing a long enough secret does not require extractable randomness. The proof is a short parity argument. The idea of the construction extends to other thresholds: for two-out-of-$n$ and $r$-out-of-$r$ sharing we give perfect schemes with $(b+1)$-bit shares, private for classes of flat sources from which no single bit can be extracted with error below $1/(4n-2)$ and $1/(2(2^r-1))$, respectively.

title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
abstract: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. evidence.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
evidence.abstract: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. Finally, a proof-of-concept 3D experiment, in which actions change the illumination of an unobserved room, shows that the paradigm can also be applied to spatial environments.
