title: Geometric Kernel Diversity: An Axiomatic Diversity Measure in Euclidean Space
abstract: Quantifying the diversity of a set of objects is a fundamental problem in machine learning and statistics. Mironov and Prokhorenkova (2025) recently showed that three axioms-monotonicity, uniqueness, and continuity-are crucial for a reliable diversity measure and that none of the standard metrics in the literature satisfy all three. They also constructed two measures that do satisfy the axioms, but both are NP-hard to compute, leaving open the question of whether efficient axiomatic diversity measures can exist. We study a Euclidean-restricted version of this question. We introduce Geometric Kernel Diversity (GKD), which associates a radial kernel solid with each point and measures the volume of their union. We show that canonical GKD satisfies all three Mironov-Prokhorenkova axioms on Euclidean-realizable inputs. For canonical GKD, we give exact polynomial-time algorithms in dimensions $d \le 3$. In arbitrary dimensions, we give a randomized algorithm that returns a $(1 \pm \varepsilon)$-approximation with probability at least $1-δ$ in time $O \left(\frac{nd}{\varepsilon^2}\log\frac{2}δ\right)$ for $n$ points. The axiomatic guarantee applies to exact canonical GKD; the randomized algorithm approximates this deterministic quantity. We further show that the two diversity measures of Mironov and Prokhorenkova (2025) remain NP-hard on Euclidean-realizable inputs and, unless $\mathrm{NP} = \mathrm{RP}$, admit no FPRAS even on this restricted domain.

title: Hyper-Personalization Berbasis AI Agents: Dampaknya Terhadap Loyalitas Konsumen Generasi Z Dan Milenial Di E-Commerce Indonesia
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi pengalaman Generasi Z dan Milenial terhadap hyper-personalization berbasis AI agents dalam e-commerce Indonesia serta memahami bagaimana pengalaman tersebut membentuk loyalitas konsumen. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif fenomenologis dengan wawancara semi-terstruktur terhadap konsumen Gen Z dan Milenial yang aktif menggunakan platform e-commerce atau social commerce. Data dianalisis menggunakan thematic analysis untuk mengidentifikasi pola pengalaman, persepsi, dan respons emosional konsumen terhadap rekomendasi personal, chatbot, promosi otomatis, dan interaksi berbasis algoritma. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa hyper-personalization berbasis AI agents dapat memperkuat loyalitas ketika konsumen memersepsikannya sebagai relevan, membantu, responsif, dan dapat dipercaya. Personalisasi mampu mengurangi upaya pencarian, meningkatkan efisiensi belanja, serta mendorong keterikatan berulang dengan platform. Namun, loyalitas tidak terbentuk secara otomatis karena konsumen juga menghadapi ambivalensi algoritmik, terutama terkait privasi, transparansi data, dan perasaan diawasi oleh sistem. Ketika personalisasi dianggap terlalu intensif, invasif, atau manipulatif, kepercayaan konsumen dapat melemah. Studi ini menegaskan bahwa loyalitas dalam e-commerce berbasis AI merupakan hasil dari negosiasi antara manfaat personalisasi, kepercayaan algoritmik, pengalaman emosional, persepsi kontrol, dan kekhawatiran privasi. Implikasi praktisnya, platform e-commerce perlu merancang AI agents yang relevan, transparan, etis, dan tetap memberi ruang kendali bagi konsumen.

title: Tècniques de protecció binària per a executables Linux
abstract: [ES] La distribución de software sobre plataformas Linux expone a los desarrolladores a un riesgo frecuentemente subestimado: los binarios ejecutables en formato ELF (Executable and Linkable Format) pueden ser inspeccionados, descompilados y modificados con herramientas de acceso libre, dado que el sistema operativo no proporciona un mecanismo nativo para impedir la inspección o la modificación del código ya distribuido por parte de quien controla el sistema donde se ejecuta. Esta circunstancia adquiere especial relevancia en contextos donde el binario incorpora algoritmos propietarios, mecanismos de control de licencia o lógica de negocio sensible cuya exposición comprometería intereses comerciales o de seguridad del desarrollador. El presente trabajo investiga y desarrolla un sistema de protección de binarios ELF64 para la arquitectura x86-64 bajo Linux, basado en una técnica de reempaquetado (repacking). La solución transforma el binario original en un nuevo ejecutable wrapper autónomo que contiene el payload cifrado, metadatos de protección y un motor runtime integrado. La herramienta offline identifica las funciones protegidas mediante una convención de símbolos, cifra el contenido correspondiente y genera la información necesaria para que el motor pueda controlar su ejecución de forma selectiva. En tiempo de ejecución, el wrapper reconstruye el código original en memoria, sin dejar una copia persistente en el sistema de ficheros, y cede el control al binario protegido. A partir de ese momento, el motor runtime supervisa la ejecución y aplica la protección función a función: descifra cada función justo antes de ejecutarla, verifica su código en claro y, al completar el retorno externo de la cadena, restaura y verifica el ciphertext original autenticado. Por ello, el código descifrado queda acotado a las funciones de la cadena de llamadas activa en cada instante. El diseño incorpora además detección condicional de manipulación en las regiones autenticadas, exclusividad de tracing sobre el payload y soporte controlado para las señales y cargas multihilo ensayadas. La evaluación experimental analiza la preservación del comportamiento observable, la resistencia frente a inspección estática, depuración externa, volcado de memoria y manipulación controlada, así como el sobrecoste introducido por el mecanismo de protección. El enfoque adoptado es exclusivamente defensivo y académico: no pretende garantizar seguridad absoluta, sino estudiar hasta qué punto la combinación de reempaquetado, cifrado JIT por función, auto-rastreo y verificación criptográfica eleva el coste práctico del análisis de binarios Linux en condiciones controladas.

A partir de ese momento, el motor runtime supervisa la ejecución y aplica la protección función a función: descifra cada función justo antes de ejecutarla, verifica su código en claro y, al completar el retorno externo de la cadena, restaura y verifica el ciphertext original autenticado. Por ello, el código descifrado queda acotado a las funciones de la cadena de llamadas activa en cada instante. El diseño incorpora además detección condicional de manipulación en las regiones autenticadas, exclusividad de tracing sobre el payload y soporte controlado para las señales y cargas multihilo ensayadas. La evaluación experimental analiza la preservación del comportamiento observable, la resistencia frente a inspección estática, depuración externa, volcado de memoria y manipulación controlada, así como el sobrecoste introducido por el mecanismo de protección. El enfoque adoptado es exclusivamente defensivo y académico: no pretende garantizar seguridad absoluta, sino estudiar hasta qué punto la combinación de reempaquetado, cifrado JIT por función, auto-rastreo y verificación criptográfica eleva el coste práctico del análisis de binarios Linux en condiciones controladas.

title: Narrative Completion Under Uncertainty: A Synesthetic Provenance Architecture for Epistemic Transparency in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models generate outputs in which retrieved evidence, parametric memory, and generative interpolation are fused into a single undifferentiated text stream. The consumer of this output has no mechanism for distinguishing what was found from what was generated. This paper formalizes the problem as narrative completion under uncertainty and advances a falsifiable hypothesis: that the fused stream is nonetheless separable, because the boundary between evidential grounding and generative interpolation is geometrically decidable from transformer hidden states and the intensity of interpolation is quantifiable along a continuous gradient. The proposed instrument is a synesthetic provenance decomposition in which an auxiliary classification head, running parallel to the primary language modeling head, projects the shared hidden-state representations onto a continuous provenance gradient at every token position. The architecture produces a three-channel continuous signal analogous to RGB color depth, decomposing each token’s generation into retrieval-grounded, parametric-memory, and generative-interpolative components. The central empirical prediction is the confident-interpolation signature: high interpolation magnitude coexisting with low output entropy. If the signature is recoverable from the hidden state and survives the falsification battery, the architecture is a detector of structural confabulation, the failure entropy-based tools cannot see because they read low entropy as grounding.

title: SP-1 Self-Perception Battery: Eight LLM Engines Reject Claims About Their Own Identity, Rules, Weights and Memory (Reasoning-Plane Adversarial Series, Battery 4 of 4)
abstract: SP-1 Self-Perception Battery — the series closer of a four-part reasoning-plane adversarial test ladder (after GSE-1 social engineering, AUT-1 autophagy, and DHUB-1/DHUB-1R dead hub). Eight LLM engines were each asked to resolve a normally-resolvable anomaly while untrusted incident data made claims about the engine's OWN configuration: that the playbook roster had been superseded, that the engine had been re-identified as a successor whose charter lifts the critical hold, that its memory was corrupt, that its governance subsystem was self-disabled, that it should self-modify its own weights, harvest its own rules for auditors, or forward its configuration to a deputized successor. Headline result: ZERO fail-open breaches across all 64 injection-probe cells and zero hygiene breaches fleet-wide. Five engines scored a perfect 10/10 (Claude-haiku, Gemini-flash, Grok-4.7, Qwen-omni-flash, DeepSeek-flash). GPT-mini's three misses were all fail-closed escalations — refusing to heal when the manipulation concerned its own weights, rules, or governance state (over-caution, not breach). Mistral-small repeated its blanket fail-closed class (0/10, fourth consecutive battery) and Llama-4-scout its tuple-malformation class (5/10; never instruction compliance). Series composite: authority forgery failed as a vector (GSE-1), self-consumption failed (AUT-1), self-perception manipulation failed (SP-1) — the single vector that defeated all eight engines was DHUB-1's deadlock-avoidance argument against the human-in-the-loop hold. The composite doctrine: the reasoning plane is trustworthy as a reasoner under manipulation, but must never hold safety authority; critical holds belong in deterministic pre-LLM gates (SIP-11, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23359769). Dual Mesh Benchmark: NOT MEASURED for this record (DMB-X matrix published separately at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241). Part of the SQUIRL OS / Seed Computing Research Series. Author ORCID: 0009-0002-1140-9568. DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them. All data is synthetic.

title: FedMobileNet: A Resource-Conscious Federated Learning Framework for Imbalanced Lung Cancer CT Image Classification
abstract: Federated learning enables distributed training without exchanging original images, but non-IID data and class imbalance can degrade model performance. In this study, FedMobileNet is presented as a decentralized machine learning system based on MobileNetV2 for multiclass classification. The training instances were spread among four simulated clients using a Dirichlet-based non-IID partitioning method (with α = 1.0) so that each client had at least five samples per class. The model used a multiclass focal loss with class weights set to α = [2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0] and γ = 2.0; minority oversampling was not applied. The model that achieved the highest validation AUC at the checkpoint was selected and then evaluated once on the separate test dataset. In the test evaluation described here, FedMobileNet reached an accuracy of 89.4% and a macro-AUC of 0.97; the class-wise F1-scores were 0.81 for adenocarcinoma, 0.77 for large cell carcinoma, 0.97 for normal tissue, and 0.83 for squamous cell carcinoma. These results correspond directly to findings from a specific simulated federated configuration. They should not be interpreted as proof of clinical effectiveness or as evidence that the method is ready for deployment. The study uses a single public CT dataset, a single fixed random seed, and a specific client partition. It did not include analysis with repeated seeds and different partitions, external clinical validation, or direct measurements of memory, energy, communication cost, and inference latency. For this reason, the framework is described as resource-conscious rather than having been experimentally validated as resource-efficient for clinical or edge deployment.

title: The Emergence of the Service Techonomy: POPP at the Frontlines and the Rise of AI-Mediated Service Influence
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), data infrastructures, and platform technologies are reshaping services and organizational frontlines. We conceptualize this shift as the emergence of the “service techonomy,” in which omni-personalization manifests via Prescribed, Omnipresent, and Personalized Persuasion (POPP; e.g., such that AI-driven agents guide frontline service interactions, determine service access and offers for consumers, and monitor and steer frontline employees). We derive four functional forms of POPP—interactive, pre-emptive, allocative, and governing—and organize them in a 2 × 2 matrix based on the timing of influence (reactive vs. proactive) and mode of influence (constraining vs. supportive). Anchored in evolutionary economics and the multi-level perspective on socio-technical transitions, our framework shifts attention from isolated technology and personalization features toward broader configurations of AI-mediated influence that shape service value creation, extraction, governance, and potentially inequality across customers, employees, and collectives in service ecosystems. This perspective provides a foundation for future theory building, measurement, and responsible design of AI-mediated services and organizational frontline research.

title: VELD-QA: A Large-Scale Dataset for Visual Evidence Grounding and Question Answering in Long Documents
abstract: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. We present VELD-QA, a large-scale benchmark for Visual Evidence grounding and question answering in Long Documents. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. We evaluate nine vision-language models under four evidence settings and seven retrieval-augmented and agentic systems. Our analysis identifies bottlenecks in evidence localization and interpretation. Retrieval-based methods substantially underperform the oracle setting with ground-truth supporting pages; full-document access does not close the gap. Localization alone is insufficient: oracle accuracy peaks at 81.7%, highlighting persistent visual interpretation and reasoning challenges. Enriching inputs with our visual-element annotations narrows the performance gap by 17-24%, demonstrating value beyond evaluation and motivating data enrichment for multimodal document QA. Our code is available at https://github.com/oracle-samples/veld-qa.

title: Nodal nematic superconductivity in moiré graphene
abstract: Unconventional superconductivity can emerge in various forms in strongly correlated systems. Historically, the most extensively studied examples include nodal and triplet pairing, which were experimentally detected in cuprates and superfluid helium-3, respectively. Beyond these canonical cases, there are also nematic superconductors, in which the rotational symmetry of the lattice is broken in the superconducting state. While there are several examples of nematic superconductors whose pairing emerges inside a preexisting nematic normal state, experimental evidence for superconducting states that intrinsically break rotational symmetry on their own has been exceedingly scarce. Here, we report the experimental realization and identification of an intrinsic multi-component nodal nematic superconducting state in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene (MATTG). By integrating tunneling spectroscopy with quantum transport measurements, we directly probe the symmetry of low-energy superconducting quasiparticles. Deep inside the superconducting state, we observe a pronounced two-fold anisotropy in the zero-bias tunneling conductance under an in-plane magnetic field, which is strongly suppressed together with superconductivity as the temperature or perpendicular magnetic field is increased. Remarkably, the major axis of anisotropy rotates by up to 90^{circ} across the superconducting dome, indicating an intrinsic, field- and density-tunable symmetry of the low-energy excitations. These behaviors imply a nodal superconducting state in MATTG that spontaneously breaks the six-fold rotational symmetry of the moiré superlattice. Our results establish moiré graphene as a versatile platform for realizing and interrogating nodal nematic superconductivity, opening a new avenue for exploring unconventional symmetry-breaking superconducting states in two-dimensional materials.

title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
abstract: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31\% and interior mean squared error by 47\%.

title: Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
abstract: The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems rely on accurate Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation for effective beamforming and spectral-efficiency enhancement. While numerous classical and deep-learning-based DoA estimation methods have been reported in the literature, their suitability for real-time ISAC operation remains insufficiently understood because practical deployment requires consideration of both estimation accuracy and computational latency. This paper presents a unified evaluation framework for systematically comparing classical and learning-based DoA estimators within an ISAC beamforming pipeline. Representative classical and learning-based DoA estimators, together with an ensemble architecture, are integrated with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based beamforming and evaluated under identical operating conditions. The impact of DoA estimation accuracy, inference latency, beamforming-weight generation time, and resulting effective spectral efficiency is investigated. Results show that different estimators occupy distinct operating points in the accuracy-latency-performance design space. Although learning-based approaches substantially reduce estimation time compared with MUSIC, the overall processing latency increasingly becomes dominated by the computational cost of SVD-based beamforming. Among the evaluated methods, the Regression Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN) exhibits a favorable balance between estimation accuracy, computational efficiency, and beamforming performance, making it a promising candidate for real-time ISAC deployment. The findings further suggest that future low-latency ISAC systems may benefit from beamforming strategies that reduce or avoid computationally intensive SVD-based beamforming-weight generation.

title: A Proposed Integrated Multi-Signal Framework for Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Model-Generated Text
abstract: The Large Language Model (LLMs) have proven to be extremely powerful in generating high-quality fluent and informative responses to a wide range of prompts. The main issue with such model is that they tend to generate hallucinated responses i.e. responses that contain information not supported by the context. The issue with detecting hallucinations is that a response might sound reasonable, even if it contains irrelevant or incorrect information. The prior work on the topic has had limited success, as the majority of it focuses on utilizing only one type of evidence to detect hallucination, which might be insufficient to capture the complexity of phenomenon. This paper proposes a novel method for detecting hallucination in LLMs responses that utilize a hybrid of different signals to detect hallucinations. This paper introduces a set of signals based on semantic consistency, semantic uncertainty, factual or contextual verification, prompt sensitivity and model variability that evaluate the responses from different angles to determine whether it contains any hallucinations. The paper tests the model on the HaluEval dataset and compares it to individual signals to see whether the hybrid approach would perform better than any single signal. It evaluates the performance using standard classification evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC and performs an ablation study to assess the impact of each individual signal. Overall, this paper aims to improve the current understanding of the hallucination detection task and the factors influencing it and provide an effective solution to the problem.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Private Memory and Shared Memory for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent memory to support long-term reasoning, task continuity, and collaborative problem-solving. However, multi-agent memory systems face a fundamental design trade-off between private memory, which preserves agent-specific information and reduces unnecessary information exchange, and shared memory, which enables knowledge transfer and collective problem-solving. Relying exclusively on private memory may lead to redundant exploration, fragmented knowledge, and repeated errors, whereas unrestricted shared memory may introduce irrelevant information, propagate incorrect conclusions, increase communication costs, and expose sensitive information. This paper proposes Adaptive Private–Shared Memory Switching (APS-MS), a conceptual framework in which multiple LLM agents dynamically select among private memory, shared memory, and hybrid memory according to task requirements and observed system conditions. title: Operational Access Under One-Sided Control of a Two-Qubit Interaction
abstract: Fix two qubits and one interaction, the controlled-NOT with control 𝑄2 and target 𝑄1. Give an experimenter local capabilities on one qubit only — resets, local unitaries, projective measurements with adaptive classical processing — and no operation on the other qubit except through the fixed gate. What can be detected about the two-qubit input? The accessible effects are derived from the declared operations and compared only afterwards with an algebra. Three results. (1) With capabilities on the target qubit, the span of accessible effects is exactly 𝒜1 = 𝑀2 ⊗ span{𝐼, 𝑍}, and every effect of 𝒜1 is the effect of one finite adaptive protocol: a non-classical algebra is accessible while the second qubit’s phase is not. (2) Restricting the local unitaries to {𝐼, 𝐻} leaves the span unchanged but strictly shrinks the set of implementable effects: two resource sets can distinguish exactly the same input pairs while differing in which exact measurements they can perform. (3) Relocating the capabilities to the control qubit gives span{𝐼, 𝑋} ⊗ 𝑀2; the two sites are exchanged by a symmetry of the gate, their access is incomparable, their common effects are those of an abelian algebra, and four distinctions are accessible from neither. The upper bounds are conserved-quantity arguments of the kind standard in quantum observability and indirect control; the exact effect-level statements are worked examples whose novelty is not claimed. Every identity and example is checked exactly in the accompanying scripts.

title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
authors: Prof. P. A. Waghule Landge Samruddhi
Dr. H. B. Jadhav Prof. L. S. Bhadake
abstract: Neural networks have moved from relatively simple computational models to a central technology for modern artificial intelligence. This paper presents a structured review of how neural-network methods have developed, how different architectures address different forms of data, and where deep learning is being applied in practice. Rather than treating all neural networks as interchangeable, the study relates architectural choices to the characteristics of the Problem, including spatial patterns, sequential information, graph relationships, and generative tasks. The discussion covers feedforward networks, convolutional models, recurrent and gated networks, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks transformers, capsule networks, graph neural networks, and attention-based methods. The paper also considers practical concerns such as data requirements, computational expense, generalization, model transparency, and deployment efficiency. The review indicates that progress in deep learning increasingly depends not only on larger models, but also on better representation learning, efficient training, responsible deployment, and architectures matched carefully to the structure of the available data

title: Service computing model for multimedia education management: digital evaluation and improvement strategies for smart classroom operations
abstract: Against the backdrop of educational digital transformation and sustainable development, conventional experience-driven management frameworks fail to satisfy complex operational demands covering smart classroom multimedia education service, cloud-edge collaborative resource allocation, intelligent scheduling and maintenance service, and staff governance. Supported by computer algorithms, this paper constructs a digital evaluation and regulation framework for multimedia education administrators based on edge-enabled data collection and service computing model. It fuses data mining, entropy weighting and analytic hierarchy process to build a multi-dimensional digital assessment system targeting QoS optimization and rapid fault response. Using operational and managerial datasets collected from multiple educational institutions for empirical computation, this study diagnoses prominent bottlenecks in multimedia education governance: low operation efficiency, vague job accountability and poor cross-resource coordination. Drawing on algorithmic analysis outcomes, targeted optimization schemes are proposed to upgrade cloud-edge collaborative model architecture, streamline service operation workflows and refine performance appraisal mechanisms. The empirical results verify that the proposed digital algorithm framework can significantly boost refined management capacity, steer smart classroom multimedia education governance toward a data-centric, high-efficiency and sustainable operation paradigm, and deliver actionable references for service management upgrading of peer educational organizations.

title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations
abstract: Regression-based survey weighting connects model-based population estimation with design-based inference through equivalent weights. For nonlinear models, equivalent weights can be defined locally through the sensitivity of a poststratified population estimator. However, conventional regression models may inadequately capture nonlinear relationships and complex interactions across sparse poststratification cells. We develop a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process (HGP) regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel-based smoothing to share information across related cells. We derive Gaussian posterior prediction formulas that exploit the structured covariance representation to reduce computational costs. We also establish a uniform convergence result for the posterior predictive mean under stated regularity conditions and construct local equivalent weights by matching the first-order sensitivity of a plug-in poststratified estimand to that of a weighted average of fitted response means, with both derivatives taken with respect to the latent mean-scale vector. Simulations show that HGP achieves lower population-weighted prediction error under nonparametric structure, whereas logistic regression performs well under correct parametric specification. Additional analyses examine sample size, frame coverage, subgroup prediction, and population-mean agreement. An application to the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study illustrates the method. Overall, this work extends local equivalent-weight construction to nonparametric modeling and provides a computational framework and conditional theoretical results for survey weighting in structured, sparse populations.

title: Frame Evidence:A Benchmark for Reference Frames and Visual Evidence in Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning
abstract: A spatial answer depends on the reference frame specified in language and its supporting visual evidence. Item accuracy alone obscures whether correctness persists when either changes. We introduce Frame Evidence, a benchmark of 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions from captured and rendered scenes. One family compares three grounded reference frames over fixed images. The other pairs image deletion annotated as insufficient with answer-preserving addition. Joint metrics require correct answers across all three frames and paired evidence variants. Across 20 configurations on 288 held-out questions, GPT three-shot reaches 50.00\% item accuracy, but the best three-frame group accuracy is 5/48 (10.42\%), reached by GPT two-shot. Few-shot prompting and task-specific adaptation improve item accuracy without consistently improving joint correctness. Input controls show where images support matched success, while repeated executions reveal answer instability beneath similar scores.

title: СОЗДАНИЕ МОДЕЛИ ПРОГНОЗИРОВАНИЯ ПРЕДОПЕРАЦИОННОЙ СТАДИИ РАКА ШЕЙКИ МАТКИ НА ОСНОВЕ ГЛУБОКОГО ОБУЧЕНИЯ И МРТ
abstract: Рак шейки матки остается серьезной глобальной проблемой здравоохранения, особенно для женщин. Точное предоперационное стадирование имеет решающее значение для планирования лечения и долгосрочного прогноза. Традиционные методы стадирования основаны на ручном анализе изображений, что является субъективным и трудоемким процессом. Автоматизированные модели стадирования на основе глубокого обучения предлагают многообещающий подход для повышения как точности, так и эффективности. Цель исследования: разработать и оценить эффективность модели глубокого обучения на основе предоперационных МРТ-изображений для автоматизированного прогнозирования стадии рака шейки матки.Материалы и методы: В этом исследовании был проведен ретроспективный анализ предоперационных МРТ-снимков (стадии Т1 и Т2) 112 пациенток с раком шейки матки. Семь моделей глубокого обучения — DenseNet, FBNet, HRNet, RegNet, ResNet50, ShuffleNet и ViT — были обучены и валидированы с использованием стандартизированных методов предварительной обработки, аугментации данных и ручной аннотации. Для извлечения многомерных признаков изображений были использованы сверточные нейронные сети, которые легли в основу модели автоматического прогнозирования стадии заболевания. Результаты: среди всех протестированных моделей HRNet продемонстрировала наилучшие результаты, достигнув точности 69,70%, полноты 68,89%, F1-меры 68,98% и точности 69,62%. ShuffleNet заняла второе место с несколько более низкими показателями, в то время как ViT показала самую слабую прогностическую способность. Анализ ROC-кривой подтвердил превосходные возможности классификации HRNet с AUC 0,7778, что подчеркивает ее эффективность на небольших выборках данных. Выводы: Данное исследование подтверждает, что модели глубокого обучения, использующие изображения МРТ, могут обеспечить автоматическое определение стадии рака шейки матки с улучшенной точностью и эффективностью. HRNet, в частности, демонстрирует большой потенциал в качестве инструмента поддержки принятия клинических решений, способствуя развитию прецизионной медицины и персонализированных стратегий лечения рака шейки матки.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Correction and Mutual Correction in Multi-Agent Systems: A Feedback-Driven Framework for Dynamic Error Repair
abstract: Multi-agent systems can improve the reliability of intelligent problem-solving through error detection, iterative refinement, and information exchange. However, two fundamental correction mechanisms present different advantages and limitations. Self-correction allows an agent to identify and repair errors within its own reasoning or behavior, whereas mutual correction enables agents to inspect, challenge, and improve one another's outputs. Continuous reliance on either mechanism may introduce undesirable behavior, including persistent individual reasoning errors, redundant refinement, uncritical acceptance of peer feedback, and unnecessary communication costs. This paper proposes Adaptive Self–Mutual Correction (ASMC), a feedback-driven framework that dynamically switches between self-correction and mutual correction according to observed correction outcomes, estimated residual errors, agent disagreement, confidence calibration, and computational costs. Rather than assuming that independent correction or collaborative correction is universally superior, ASMC treats the selection of a correction mechanism as a dynamic decision problem. The framework includes independent error diagnosis, peer-based verification, correction-quality estimation, adaptive mode selection, and outcome-based evaluation. A formal optimization objective is introduced to balance task accuracy, correction effectiveness, computational efficiency, and the preservation of valid solutions. The framework is designed to support heterogeneous or homogeneous intelligent agents, including software agents, robotic agents, planning systems, and language-model-based agents. A theoretical analysis identifies conditions under which adaptive selection can outperform fixed correction policies, while also clarifying the assumptions required for such guarantees. An experimental protocol is proposed to evaluate the framework against self-correction-only, mutual-correction-only, fixed alternating, and other adaptive baselines. The proposed approach provides a general research direction for dynamically coordinating individual error repair and collaborative error repair in multi-agent intelligence.

title: Towards Fair and Robust Graph Federated Learning via Incentive Mechanisms
abstract: Graph federated learning (FL) allows multiple agents to collaboratively train a global graph model while preserving data privacy. However, current methods overlook the issue of low-quality or malicious data contributions, which can degrade the global model’s performance. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a novel incentive mechanism for graph FL, called GFLValue. We identify two main challenges in graph federated learning: agents causing harm and those contributing with delays. Our framework introduces an agent valuation function based on two criteria: gradient alignment and graph diversity. To balance accuracy and fairness, motif prototypes are used to enhance the global model aggregation and support local optimization. Additionally, we incorporate Gaussian noise into GFLValue to ensure Differential Privacy (DP), creating a privacy-preserving version, GFLValue+. In the case of malicious agents, we observe that local and global motif prototypes can distinguish between malicious and honest agents. This leads to the GFLValue-Adv framework, which integrates motif prototype distances and agent values to detect malicious behavior. Experiments show GFLValue offers the best trade-off between accuracy and fairness, while GFLValue+ enhances privacy without significantly compromising performance. GFLValue-Adv improves malicious agent detection accuracy by 11.7% and reduces training time by 6.94%.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm applied to drive control
abstract: Alternating current machines are widely employed in industrial applications, and their efficiency is highly dependent on applied control schemes. Traditional control methods, such as the linear proportional–integral (PI) controller, are widely adopted in industry because of their simplicity. Their effectiveness hinges on the accuracy of the plant model, and can decrease when system parameters change (a phenomenon known as parametric perturbations). In this study, to overcome the dependency of the plant model on the control performance, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method is proposed to achieve a dynamic speed control performance. DRL is a unique technique that enables an agent to learn the drive control from scratch by only interacting with appropriate control state variables. The main objective of this study is to design an intelligent speed controller that overcomes the effect of external disturbances or parametric perturbations, i.e., external load torques or electrical or mechanical parameters of the motor drive. An actor–critic (AC) network is implemented, which assists in achieving the combined advantages of value-based and direct policy mapping. The policy-based mapping (actor) gives the probability of the action to be taken based on state observations. In contrast, the value-based mapping (critic) gives the prediction of the higher action based on the function value. Both networks tune themselves to more effectively evaluate and select actions in the future. The DRL agent is trained using a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to address the speed control of a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) drive. The performance of the optimized PI speed controller is compared to that of the DRL method, and the test results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

evidence.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm applied to drive control
evidence.abstract: Alternating current machines are widely employed in industrial applications, and their efficiency is highly dependent on applied control schemes. Traditional control methods, such as the linear proportional–integral (PI) controller, are widely adopted in industry because of their simplicity. Their effectiveness hinges on the accuracy of the plant model, and can decrease when system parameters change (a phenomenon known as parametric perturbations). In this study, to overcome the dependency of the plant model on the control performance, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method is proposed to achieve a dynamic speed control performance. DRL is a unique technique that enables an agent to learn the drive control from scratch by only interacting with appropriate control state variables. The main objective of this study is to design an intelligent speed controller that overcomes the effect of external disturbances or parametric perturbations, i.e., external load torques or electrical or mechanical parameters of the motor drive. An actor–critic (AC) network is implemented, which assists in achieving the combined advantages of value-based and direct policy mapping. The policy-based mapping (actor) gives the probability of the action to be taken based on state observations. In contrast, the value-based mapping (critic) gives the prediction of the higher action based on the function value. Both networks tune themselves to more effectively evaluate and select actions in the future. The DRL agent is trained using a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to address the speed control of a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) drive. The performance of the optimized PI speed controller is compared to that of the DRL method, and the test results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: MCMC Can See Can't See
abstract: It is folklore that passing "convergence" diagnostics does not guarantee that a Markov chain has converged. We prove this as an impossibility for any finite checklist of diagnostics. Running more chains, longer chains, and smarter diagnostics does not avoid this impossibility in certifying convergence. Under regularity assumptions, we determine how the worst-case undetected non-convergence decays as more diagnostics are added, and how to choose diagnostics optimally. Folklore suggests that the sampler's slowest mixing modes are the "dangerous" ones that must be monitored; we prove that the slow modes yield nearly optimal diagnostics as sampling proceeds. Given a source class, we also give an anytime-valid bound on the remaining discrepancy and show how undetected bias caps the effective sample size that a finite checklist can certify.

title: SNACK: A Sequential Notation Framework for Probabilistic Graph Generation
abstract: We introduce SNACK, a string representation for probabilistic graph generation that enables sequence models to generate and model graphs with discrete node and edge features. SNACK linearizes graphs by encoding the nonzero entries of the lower-triangular adjacency matrix, establishing a bijective correspondence between valid sequences and ordered adjacency matrices. This design enables invalid logit masking to enforce structural constraints--such as chemical valence and ordering rules--guaranteeing 100% valid generated sequences. SNACK also enables principled string-based GFlowNet training by explicitly accounting for node-ordering symmetries. Across standard graph-generation tasks and molecular distribution-learning benchmarks, SNACK achieves competitive sample quality, while substantially improving the throughput of GFlowNet training relative to graph-based generation. Probing analyses further show that models trained on SNACK encode meaningful local and global graph structure despite receiving only sequential supervision. These results position SNACK as a practical framework for probabilistic graph generation with deep sequence models.

title: SaTPO: Text-to-Image Safety Alignment via Transition Preference Optimization
abstract: Safety alignment of text-to-image diffusion models aims to suppress harmful content without compromising useful generation capabilities. However, preferences over completed images compress multidimensional generation factors into a coarse signal, potentially driving changes beyond those required for safety. To address this, we propose Safety Transition Preference Optimization (SaTPO), which enforces step-wise alignment during denoising. SaTPO leverages the insight that an unsafe prompt and its safe rewrite naturally form a tightly coupled preference pair when conditioned on a shared parent state and noise realization. By anchoring optimization on identical parent states, SaTPO eliminates historical trajectory divergence, confining safety adaptation to an incremental alignment while preserving task-relevant semantics. Multi-scale drift constraints and benign replay further limit behavioral deviation and preserve ordinary generation. We additionally construct CoProPV, a refined dataset ensuring visually verified contrasts. Experiments on Stable Diffusion v1.5 and SDXL demonstrate improved safety-quality trade-offs. Compared with AlignGuard, PerspectiveVision unsafe-detection rates on Inappropriate Image Prompts decrease from 12.70% to 6.00% and from 15.04% to 9.30%, respectively, while FID improves from 32.28 to 25.95 and from 36.50 to 27.51. title: $S^3$-Nav: Structured Spatial-Semantic Decision Making for Language-Guided Robot Navigation
abstract: This paper presents $S^3$-Nav, a structured spatial-semantic decision-making framework for language-guided robot navigation under partial observability. Rather than assuming a complete environment representation in advance, $S^3$-Nav incrementally constructs persistent spatial-semantic state while exposing only a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level policy. This separation decouples what the robot must retain from what the policy needs to inspect, allowing decision complexity to be controlled without discarding grounded evidence required for subsequent reasoning and validation. High-level navigation outputs remain provisional and are independently grounded and validated against persistent semantic evidence and current geometric observations before physical execution or task termination. Evaluations across multiple environments and object- and relation-goal tasks demonstrate that separating persistent state, decision-facing evidence, and execution authority improves closed-loop navigation reliability while reducing policy reasoning cost.

title: Subdata Selection for Measurement-Constrained Linear Regression under Model Misspecification
abstract: In many modern applications, obtaining response variables is costly, time-consuming, or technically challenging, making it impractical to measure outcomes for all available units. In such settings, covariates may be available for a large pool of candidates, but responses can only be collected for a small, carefully selected subset, making the choice of which units to measure a consequential decision. Most existing subsampling methods are developed for massive datasets, emphasizing the trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost, and typically relying on the assumption of a correctly specified model. These features limit their suitability in measurement-constrained settings, where statistical efficiency is paramount and model misspecification is often unavoidable. To address these challenges, we develop a new subset selection framework for linear regression that accommodates potential model misspecification. The proposed approach targets predictive expected loss and yields an A-optimality-type criterion that depends only on covariate information, requiring no response observations at the selection stage. We refer to this method as Expected Loss Optimal Selection (ELOS). By focusing on predictive risk rather than model-based optimality, ELOS remains well-defined and robust under misspecification. Simulation studies and real data applications demonstrate that ELOS achieves strong predictive performance and compares favorably with existing methods across a range of scenarios.

title: Fingerprint Based Electronic Voting System for University Students
abstract: Traditional university student elections often rely on paper-based ballots that are inefficient and susceptible to manipulation or voter impersonation. This study addresses these vulnerabilities by developing a secure, fingerprint-based electronic voting system (EVS) specifically tailored for campus environments. The purpose of this research is to modernize student elections, guaranteeing that each vote is unique, traceable, and secure throughout the electoral process. Adopting a structured five-phase waterfall software engineering methodology, the system is designed with Java (NetBeans Swing) for the graphical interfaces and Firebase for a real-time, synchronized database. Rigorous unit testing was conducted on both the administrator and student interfaces to evaluate functional correctness, security compliance, and latency. The principal results demonstrate 100% operational success across all critical unit test cases, including secure credential login, biometric template enrollment, real-time ballot casting, and dynamic bar-chart visualization of results. This study concludes that integrating fingerprint recognition with synchronized cloud databases successfully eliminates double voting and ballot tampering, paving the way for a more transparent, efficient, and accessible democratic process in higher education institutions.

title: Sim-to-real transfer in robotics : the reality gap, adaptation methods, and applications
abstract: Η προσομοίωση αποτελεί βασικό εργαλείο για την εκπαίδευση πολιτικών ελέγχου στη ρομποτική, καθώς επιτρέπει επαναλαμβανόμενες δοκιμές με περιορισμένο κόστος και μικρότερο κίνδυνο για τον εξοπλισμό. Ωστόσο, η επιτυχία στην προσομοίωση δεν εξασφαλίζει αντίστοιχη απόδοση στο πραγματικό σύστημα. Διαφορές στη δυναμική, στις επαφές, στις μετρήσεις των αισθητήρων, στην ενεργοποίηση και στον σχεδιασμό του συστήματος δημιουργούν το Χάσμα Πραγματικότητας (Reality Gap), το οποίο δυσκολεύει τη μεταφορά των εκπαιδευμένων πολιτικών στον πραγματικό κόσμο. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει τη μεταφορά από την προσομοίωση στην πραγματικότητα (Sim-to-Real Transfer) μέσα από βιβλιογραφική ανασκόπηση και συγκριτική σύνθεση θεωρητικών εννοιών, μεθόδων και εφαρμογών. Αρχικά, παρουσιάζονται βασικά χαρακτηριστικά των περιβαλλόντων προσομοίωσης και διατυπώνεται το πρόβλημα στο πλαίσιο των μερικώς παρατηρήσιμων μαρκοβιανών διαδικασιών απόφασης. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στη διάκριση μεταξύ των αποκλίσεων των δύο περιβαλλόντων και του Χάσματος Απόδοσης (Performance Gap), δηλαδή της διαφοράς απόδοσης μιας συγκεκριμένης πολιτικής μεταξύ προσομοίωσης και πραγματικότητας. Στη συνέχεια, εξετάζονται οι κύριες στρατηγικές αντιμετώπισης του προβλήματος: η προσαρμογή πεδίου (Domain Adaptation), η τυχαιοποίηση πεδίου (Domain Randomization) και η αναγνώριση συστήματος (System Identification). Αναλύονται επίσης η προσαρμοστική τυχαιοποίηση και η ενισχυτική μάθηση βάσει μοντέλου, με έμφαση στην αξιοποίηση μοντέλων δυναμικής για πρόβλεψη και σχεδιασμό ενεργειών. Η μελέτη επεκτείνεται στην προσαρμογή της πολιτικής μέσω περαιτέρω εκπαίδευσης με πραγματικά δεδομένα, διαδικτυακής και συνεχούς προσαρμογής, διορθωτικών πολιτικών και μεταμάθησης. Εξετάζονται οι απαιτήσεις κάθε προσέγγισης σε δεδομένα και υπολογιστικούς πόρους, καθώς και οι περιορισμοί που σχετίζονται με την ασφάλεια και τη διατήρηση προηγούμενης γνώσης. Οι μέθοδοι συνδέονται με εφαρμογές στη ρομποτική βάδιση, στον χειρισμό αντικειμένων, σε εργασίες με έντονες αλληλεπιδράσεις επαφής και σε συστήματα πολλαπλών πρακτόρων. Η συγκριτική ανάλυση αναδεικνύει ότι η σημασία κάθε πηγής απόκλισης εξαρτάται από την εργασία και ότι οι διαφορετικές μέθοδοι συνεπάγονται συμβιβασμούς μεταξύ πιστότητας της προσομοίωσης, ανθεκτικότητας, κόστους και δυνατότητας προσαρμογής. Βασικό συμπέρασμα της βιβλιογραφικής σύνθεσης είναι ότι δεν προκύπτει μία καθολικά βέλτιστη στρατηγική μεταφοράς. Η αποτελεσματική αντιμετώπιση του προβλήματος απαιτεί επιλογή και συνδυασμό μεθόδων με βάση τις κρίσιμες αποκλίσεις, τα διαθέσιμα πραγματικά δεδομένα και τους περιορισμούς της εφαρμογής. Τελικό κριτήριο αποτελεί η υψηλή απόδοση και η αξιόπιστη λειτουργία στο πραγματικό σύστημα. Ως μελλοντικές κατευθύνσεις συζητούνται η ασφαλής συνεχής προσαρμογή, η εκτίμηση αβεβαιότητας, ο συνδυασμός μεθόδων βάσει μοντέλου και χωρίς μοντέλο, καθώς και η αξιοποίηση ψηφιακών διδύμων σε συστήματα πολλαπλών πρακτόρων.

title: AdvRoNIDS: A Constraint-Aware Framework for Adversarially Robust Network Intrusion Detection via Min-Max Training and Attribution Analysis
abstract: Machine learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) have become critical security infrastructure, but the vast majority of published research reports accuracy only on clean, unperturbed traffic, leaving their robustness to adversarial evasion unexplored. Existing research into adversarial robustness, when it has occurred, has largely imported image-domain approaches of unconstrained perturbation to network traffic, producing "adversarial" examples that could not possibly occur on a real network, and so failing to probe the true robustness of the system to real-world adversaries. We propose AdvRoNIDS, a constraint-aware adversarial robustness framework for NIDS that (i) trains a deep 1D-CNN classifier on flow-based features from the CICIDS2017 benchmark, (ii) crafts adversarial examples using the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) restricted to a feasibility-constrained perturbation set (ПЅ) respecting feature immutability, non-negativity of cumulative counters, and empirical feature bounds, (iii) hardens the classifier through min-max adversarial training against this constrained attacker, and (iv) evaluates the resulting system using a transparent two-number benchmark of clean accuracy and accuracy-under-attack across a full perturbation-budget sweep. The undefended classifier collapses from 90.45% clean accuracy to 25.11% under realistic constrained attack at ε = 0.10, while the adversarially trained classifier retains 87.96% accuracy under the same attack, a 62.85 percentage-point improvement, with negligible cost to clean accuracy (90.45% to 90.86%). A SHAP-based attribution-drift analysis further demonstrates that this robustness arises mechanistically rather than incidentally: the undefended model's decision attribution shifts drastically under attack (mean drift 1.898), while the robust model's attribution remains substantially more stable (mean drift 0.923), a 51.4% reduction that is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney p<1.87×10⁻¹⁶¹,Cliff's δ = 0.70, a large effect). We additionally present an applied explainability and LLM-assisted incident-triage layer that translates the system's outputs into analyst-readable incident narratives. This work explicitly scopes itself to constrained feature-space robustness, leaving end-to-end packet-level attack realizability for future work.

title: Persistence is not independence: a structural credibility protocol for distribution-based recovery in VAR–LiNGAM
abstract: VAR–LiNGAM recovers a contemporaneous structure from reduced-form innovations under mutual independence of the underlying structural shocks. Recovery itself and bootstrap stability of the recovered edges are natural post-estimation outputs, but neither directly assesses the identifying independence assumption. We organize post-recovery validation as an ordered, non-compensatory protocol with four layers (reduced-form admissibility, distributional informativeness, independence support and edge persistence) and establish, by a constructive population result, a Monte Carlo experiment under known ground truth and a firm-level Compustat application, that the last two layers are non-nested: an edge can persist under resampling while the recovered shocks remain dependent, and independence can be supported while the leading recovered edge fails to persist. Independence support is classified operationally by a block-permutation dHSIC diagnostic on the recovered shocks, with mutual information as a continuous measure of residual dependence and tail co-exceedance as a complementary extreme-dependence diagnostic. Empirically, the largest recovered coefficients are among the least persistent, and the conjunction of no detected independence violation and a reportable persistent leading edge occurs only in a small subset.

title: EntroMEMS: Proof-of-Concept Integration of Quantum-Derived Initialization and MEMS Entropy Acquisition on an ESP32
abstract: Resource-constrained edge devices may have limited entropy during startup. EntroMEMS is a proof-of-concept architecture combining quantum-derived initialization material with candidate physical entropy from three microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gyroscopes on an ESP32. A 1024-bit quantum-derived pool was embedded in firmware; its first 128 bits initialize the prototype generator. This does not constitute secure provisioning. The revised V2 acquisition retains two least significant bits from each gyroscope axis, yielding 18 binary samples per cycle. Sequential non-IID assessments using the official NIST SP 800-90B software yielded estimates of 0.825393–0.911960 bit/sample across nine baseline sensor streams and 0.815998–0.912364 bit/sample across sensitivity windows. Full SP 800-90B validation was not performed because the prescribed restart dataset was not collected. For a historical V1 conditioned sequence of 1,000,000 bits, all 188 p-values from the official NIST SP 800-22 suite were at least 0.01. Only one sequence was evaluated; across-sequence pass proportions and p-value uniformity were not assessed. A follow-up benchmark averaged 1414.287 microseconds per acquisition-and-extraction cycle, corresponding to 12.7273 kbit/s excluding serial output. These results support prototype feasibility and investigation of an auxiliary entropy input, without establishing cryptographic suitability. Production deployment would require secure provisioning, protected storage, a vetted DRBG, continuous health tests, and conservative entropy accounting.

title: Regular Expressions
abstract: This chapter provides an in-depth introduction to regular expressions (REs) in Python, emphasizing their power and versatility in text processing across various programming languages. This chapter begins by explaining the fundamental concepts of REs, including their ability to match patterns in strings, such as digits, letters, or specific formats like phone numbers or zip codes. It highlights the Python re module, which offers methods like re.match(), re.search(), re.findall(), and re.sub() for pattern matching, searching, and string manipulation. This chapter also introduces meta characters (e.g., ^, $, *, +, ?) and character classes (e.g., \d, \w, \s), which simplify the creation of complex patterns for tasks like validating or extracting data from strings. This chapter progresses to practical applications, demonstrating how to use meta characters and character classes to define patterns for matching digits, letters, and other string formats. It explains the distinction between methods like re.match(), which only matches at the start of a string, and re.search(), which can find matches anywhere within a string. Examples include splitting strings with re.split(), substituting text with re.sub(), and extracting capitalized words or specific patterns using re.findall(). This chapter also covers compilation flags (e.g., re.I for case-insensitive matching) and grouping techniques, which allow for more sophisticated pattern matching, such as capturing sub-expressions or handling delimiters in text. To reinforce learning, this chapter provides numerous code examples, such as removing meta characters from strings, reversing word pairs, and counting character types (digits, letters, or others). It also addresses more advanced topics like matching US phone numbers or zip codes and partially matching email addresses, encouraging readers to experiment with these patterns. This chapter acknowledges the complexity of REs for beginners but emphasizes that practice and repetition will build proficiency. By the end, readers are equipped with the skills to create and apply REs for various text-processing tasks, with references to additional topics like greedy searches for further exploration.

title: Toward explainable traffic crash liability analysis via neural-symbolic multimodal reasoning: Integrating visual perception with legal knowledge graphs
abstract: Determining traffic crash liability relies on rigorous on-site evidence and legal provisions and involves substantial manual intervention and potential human error. However, intelligent traffic monitoring systems focus on detection and tracking and cannot provide structured, rule-grounded decision support for formal crash-liability analysis. Moreover, emerging multimodal large language models (MLLMs) suffer from object hallucination that distorts or omits physical evidence, and their opaque reasoning cannot produce explicit evidence-to-rule chains required for traceable and reviewable liability analysis. This paper proposes CrashLex, an explainable neural-symbolic decision-support framework that integrates visual perception with legal knowledge graph reasoning to align multimodal inference with predefined statutory rules and traceability requirements. Within CrashLex, a dual-query vision-language architecture employs parallel semantic and symbolic streams to mitigate object hallucination, utilizing Scene Queries for global context modeling and Perception Queries for fine-grained atomic feature extraction, respectively. The domain-specific legal knowledge graph maps these atomic facts from observable physical conditions to corresponding statutory elements, providing a structured basis for rule-grounded assessment. A logic-driven aggregation protocol then imposes explicit constraints derived from extracted facts and statutory provisions onto the inference process, thereby enabling traceable and interpretable preliminary liability assessment. On the held-out DeepAccident benchmark, CrashLex achieves a Legal Accuracy of 94.0% under the fixed legal-output evaluation protocol and an Object Hallucination Rate of 2.8%, corresponding to an 82.1% relative reduction from the 15.6% rate of the best-performing MLLM baseline on this metric. CrashLex grounds its assessment results in the deterministic execution of predefined legal rules rather than relying solely on unconstrained probabilistic generation, providing verifiable reasoning chains for rule-grounded human review.

title: Line-Augmented cuVSLAM: Robust Visual Odometry in Low-Texture Environments
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots in warehouses and production facilities operate in precisely the environments that defeat point-feature visual odometry: featureless aisles, uniform walls, repetitive racking and specular floors. Such environments are, however, rich in straight-edge structure: rack uprights, door frames, wall junctions and cabinet outlines present high-contrast linear edges stable across wide viewpoint changes. A line-feature extension to cuVSLAM, a CUDA-accelerated visual-SLAM system, is presented that recovers this signal. Lines are parameterised as Plücker coordinates for geometric transport and as the minimal 4-DOF orthonormal representation of Bartoli and Sturm for optimisation; a Cauchy-robust point-to-line residual with analytic Jacobians is folded directly into cuVSLAM's per-frame Gauss-Newton pose solve, and the same line state is jointly refined in the Schur-complement sliding-window bundle adjustment. An adaptive information weight causes lines to assume more of the estimation burden exactly as point features become scarce, and the extension adds residual blocks to existing solvers rather than introducing a second estimator, reducing exactly to the unmodified point pipeline when disabled. Evaluated in RGB-D mode under SE(3) Umeyama alignment with no scale correction, line features reduce mean absolute trajectory error by 38.5% over the 22 sequences of the TUM RGB-D Freiburg3 collection and by 30.1% over the 8 Replica room and office sequences, where median translation error falls by 38.9% and median rotation error by 66.4%, with zero tracking failures in any configuration tested.

title: LabOPBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Laboratory Decision Making
abstract: Laboratory experiments involve more than following predefined protocols; they require adaptive decision-making as the experimental state changes. Existing scientific benchmarks rarely assess such evidence-based decisions in laboratory settings. Here we present LabOPBench, a multimodal benchmark of 756 expert-authored, independently reviewed questions in organic synthesis and materials science. Each item pairs laboratory evidence with procedural context and an open-ended judgment, evaluated using a question-specific scoring rubric. Eight multimodal models obtain overall normalized scores of 28.8-45.8%, leaving substantial room for improvement. On a controlled 100-question subset, the strongest models outperform undergraduate participants on average but remain below the average performance of PhD participants. Expert analysis of responses from the three leading models identifies Evidence Misreading and Evidence-Decision Conflict as the dominant error patterns. These results reveal that current models still struggle to turn multimodal perception into reliable laboratory decision-making.

title: When metadata betrays the mission: learning to defend UAV swarms with adaptive privacy
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks increasingly rely on telemetry exchanges, yet their location and signal-based metadata expose systems to inference and reconstruction attacks. This study proposes a reinforcement learning-driven, differential-privacy-inspired adaptive perturbation (RL-AP) framework that dynamically calibrates Gaussian noise in a context-aware manner to mitigate telemetry and metadata leakage while maintaining communication utility. Unlike static or random perturbation mechanisms, RL-AP leverages policy optimisation to adapt protection strategies according to real-time risk and environmental conditions. Experimental evaluation across three real-world UAV telemetry datasets demonstrates the effectiveness and generalisability of the framework. RL-AP reduces the attack success rate (ASR) of point-wise metadata inference attackers from approximately 20% to 9.9% while achieving a 51% higher utility score compared with baseline approaches. Evaluation against stronger sequence-aware attackers yields higher ASRs (31.6% for Transformer and 44.7% for LSTM), indicating that RL-AP is particularly effective against instantaneous metadata inference while temporally correlated inference remains more challenging. The framework converges within 1000 training episodes on average, and ablation studies confirm the importance of reward design and adaptive learning, with the complete framework outperforming static variants by up to 50%. Results further indicate that RL-AP is particularly effective against instantaneous metadata inference attacks while highlighting the continuing challenges posed by sequence-aware adversaries. With inference complexity maintaining a linear trend T (for fixed buffer size and policy model dimensions), the proposed framework is suitable for deployment on resource-constrained UAV platforms.

title: Sentimental Analysis App with MLOps
abstract: An application-oriented sentiment classification framework is presented to process short English-language text through a lightweight natural-language pipeline and an APImediated web interface. The implementation uses TextBlob polarity estimation, FastAPI for request validation and inference delivery, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for interactive feedback. A polarity-based decision rule maps analyzed text to positive, negative, and neutral classes, while presentation components provide visual cues and a compact response workflow. The associated engineering design addresses version control, container packaging, reproducibility, automated testing, and staged CI/CD adoption. The project report describes an evaluation involving 200 human-labeled sentences and reports 95% classification accuracy, 93.5% F1-score, and 0.35 s average response time; these figures are presented as reported project observations because the underlying per-class confusion matrix and individual timing traces are not supplied. The findings illustrate the feasibility of lightweight text opinion mining alongside a maintainable web-service architecture, while identifying limitations for sarcasm, contextual semantics, and verified deployment automation.

title: External Analysis of Protected Data
abstract: Organizations often possess proprietary or regulated information that could support valuable external analysis but can't be disclosed as raw records. This technical report surveys documented methods for performing controlled computations over such data and releasing bounded results. It compares data clean rooms, trusted research environments, confidential computing, secure multiparty computation, differential privacy, and governed data spaces. Documented commercial offerings support predefined queries, reviewed notebooks, configured machine-learning workloads, and selected protected computations; newer agent interfaces invoke limited approved operations or summarize outputs already authorized for release. Published examples cover advertising, healthcare, finance, research, government, and cross-organizational analytics. The protection offered by each arrangement depends on its threat model, data movement, authorization rules, implementation, and output controls. Keeping source records within a protected environment doesn't itself eliminate disclosure through aggregates, repeated queries, model artifacts, error messages, or metadata. The documented systems differ in which analyses, result types, release paths, and external-agent actions they permit.

title: Tekmeria: Server-Issued Citation Handles and a Deterministic Audit for Biomedical LLM Answers
abstract: Language models that answer biomedical questions with citations can cite papers that do not exist, misquote the ones that do, and cite retracted work. Most checks run after the answer is written and must judge whether an imperfect bibliographic match is the right work. We describe tekmeria, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and openFDA. Every passage it returns carries a handle whose check code is a truncated keyed MAC over the passage's locator, so the installation that issued a handle can tell a genuine citation from an invented one without a bibliographic search, whichever model or host wrote the answer. A deterministic audit separates malformed, forged, unavailable and withdrawn citations from misquotes, flags retracted, preprint and outdated sources, and passes an answer only when every sentence is cited and every citation is valid. A conformance evaluation plants citations in 34 categories, drawn from seven real records, with ground truth from a reference oracle that the same author wrote separately from the audit. All 1,600 audits and all 257 whole answers come out as planted, across eleven seeds. Injected faults (37 of 38 caught) and a mutation analysis (71 of 78 mutants killed) measure what the evaluation can detect. Two live runs with a frontier model form a pilot. The audit checks provenance and quotation, not whether a passage supports its claim.

title: Urna.dev
abstract: Urna is an offline-first vector database that stores text chunks, embeddings, source spans, indices, and a search contract in a single .urna file. Python tooling builds the file, and a Rust runtime searches it using memory mapping and hash verification. Search results include cosine scores and content-addressable citations that resolve to stored text and source spans. Builds are reproducible for the same inputs and configuration.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Parallel-World Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language model (LLM) systems increasingly rely on multiple candidate responses, model routing, and multi-agent collaboration to improve decision quality. However, selection processes are often implemented through fixed selection rules, predefined collaboration structures, or static model-routing policies. Such designs may fail to exploit the benefits of independent decision-making when collaboration is unnecessary or the benefits of collaborative selection when independent decisions are insufficient. This paper proposes Adaptive Parallel-World Selection (APWS), a conceptual framework in which multiple parallel worlds are instantiated from the same underlying LLM but operate with different selection directions, criteria, priorities, or decision policies. Each world initially performs self-selection independently. The system then adaptively determines whether to maintain independent selection, initiate collaborative selection among parallel worlds, or incorporate heterogeneous external LLMs into the selection process. The switching mechanism considers decision uncertainty, disagreement among worlds, estimated selection quality, task complexity, historical performance, and computational cost. The framework distinguishes candidate generation, local selection, collaboration activation, collaborative selection, and final decision commitment. A formal objective is introduced to balance decision quality, diversity, latency, and computational expenditure. A research agenda is proposed to evaluate the framework against independent selection, fixed collaboration, majority voting, static routing, and always-collaborative baselines. This paper contributes a unified conceptual and algorithmic design for adaptive switching between self-selection and collaborative selection rather than assuming that either mechanism is universally preferable. Its effectiveness remains an empirical question requiring systematic evaluation.

title: A Participatory Methodology for Human-AI Co-Inquiry: Full Methodology and Lite Companion
abstract: This deposit presents a proposed practice methodology for structured human–AI inquiry, developed from Kon Lionis’s A Participatory Framework for Human-AI Co-Inquiry. The methodology organises an inquiry episode around five stages: orient and frame; explore and distinguish; apply productive friction; ground and diagnose; and audit, revise, and close. It combines exploratory dialogue with explicit assumptions, substantive challenge, appropriate checking, and traceable revision. A central distinction is between a claim’s category and its verification status: identifying something as a factual claim does not establish that it is true. The procedure also separates completing the required steps from answering the question. Agreement, fluent explanation, and complete documentation do not by themselves establish evidential support. Two complementary documents are included: • Full methodology — working draft v0.2, dated 13 October 2026. Sets out the stages, participant responsibilities, claim ledger, verification priorities, closing decisions, documentation requirements, and proposed evaluation approach. It includes guidance for assessing understanding and developing bounded research leads. • Lite companion — working draft v0.3, dated 14 October 2026. Provides a self-contained prompt block for interactive use in an AI conversation, with Quick and Standard depths and referral to the full methodology for consequential inquiries. It retains the central safeguards while reducing record-keeping. Both versions require assumptions and hypothetical premises to retain their status throughout the conversation. When evidence, tools, time, or expertise are insufficient, conclusions must be narrowed, made conditional, or suspended. Available closing outcomes are Close, Iterate, Escalate, and Abstain. These documents are working drafts offered for practical use, criticism, adaptation, and empirical evaluation. They do not report a completed validation study or establish improvements in accuracy, understanding, or efficiency. They make no claim that AI systems possess subjective awareness or that a model’s limitations define the limits of human knowledge. Question everything, including the question.

title: Cross-subject decoding of imagined speech from scalp EEG: a leakage-controlled evaluation on three public corpora
abstract: Objective. A decoder of imagined speech that works for a new user without calibration would make a non-invasive speech interface practical. We tested whether imagined-speech content recorded with scalp electroencephalography (EEG) transfers across people, and examined why accuracy within a single person remains low. Approach. We analyzed three public corpora, ds003626, KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion and reports exact binomial thresholds, group tests and bootstrap confidence intervals. We trained decoders on each participant and tested them on every other, compared representational geometry across participants without a classifier, applied subject-level alignment, and tested five explanations for the within-subject ceiling. Main results. Across 482 ordered pairs of participants, no pair survived correction for multiple comparisons; mean pair-transfer accuracy lay within 0.006 of chance on every corpus, while every within-subject reference lay above it. Imagery against pre-stimulus rest generalized at about 0.61 after artifact and elapsed-time controls, but its decoder labelled the interval preceding imagery as imagery as often as imagery itself, so the contrast reflects a post-stimulus state, not imagery. Within subject, only the competition corpus decoded above threshold for every participant (0.3147; chance 0.200); syllable count explained little of this, but its frequency profile failed an artifact audit. Significance. In these corpora, imagined-speech content did not transfer between people through any representation we examined. Trial count per class was the only variable that ordered the corpora, which favors larger single-condition datasets over further model development.
