title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.

title: The Context Coordinate System and the Principle of Unbroken Memory (컨텍스트 좌표계와 끊기지 않는 기억의 원리)
abstract: The fundamental physical constraint of long-horizon large language model (LLM) agent systems is that the Active Context Window is finite. Prevailing agent frameworks rely on Summary-based Compaction, overwriting the existing dialogue history with a generative summary. However, this destroys the return address to the original log, provides no conservation check for omitted items, and severs the Continuity of the Present in the middle of ongoing work. This paper proposes Context Lattice, an address-based memory management architecture built on the Context Coordinate System, Reference-based Folding, and Asynchronous Stepped Window Shifts:(1) Immutable Raw Log & 5-Level Canonical Coordinates with mathematical Conservation Equations enforced by deterministic runtime code;(2) 5-Slot Frequency-Ordered Window Partitioning and Tier-1 Folding of completed tool payloads (85–95% of context volume) into 1-line coordinate pointers with Append-at-Tail lossless dereferencing;(3) Asynchronous Pre-building and Idle-Boundary Atomic Stepped Shifts to preserve prompt prefix (KV) cache stability and unbroken working memory. Across four quantitative studies using real agent development transcripts and our open-source deterministic coordinate engine (context-lattice), canonical coordinate dereferencing achieves 100.0% recall on 20 ground-truth probes (vs. 30.0% on compaction summary alone and 40.0% with kept pre-compaction messages), reduces context volume by 79–91% with 0% dialogue loss (~8.6–9x longer single-window span), achieves a 95.9% prompt prefix cache hit rate over 100 turns, and processes 50,000 log lines (10,000 turns) in ~185–260 ms with 0% integrity error. --- [한국어 초록]본 논문은 기존 덮어쓰기 요약 압축(Summary-based Compaction)이 야기하는 역참조 주소 상실, 무결성 검증 부재, 작업 중 '현재 맥락의 단절' 문제를 해결하기 위해, 5계층 정준 컨텍스트 좌표계(Context Coordinate System)와 참조 기반 도구 폴딩(Reference Folding), 휴지기 계단식 윈도우 전환(Stepped Window Shift)에 기반한 기억 관리 구조(Context Lattice)를 제안하고 실증한다. (한국어 및 영어 전문 PDF, 1분 개념 영상 수록)

title: EVALUATING THE ACCURACY OF MACHINE TRANSLATION BETWEEN ENGLISH AND UZBEK: A COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS APPROACH
abstract: This article investigates the empirical evaluation of machine translation (MT) systems operating between English and Uzbek, analyzing performance across neural, statistical, and hybrid translation architectures. The typological divergence between analytical, head-initial English and agglutinative, head-final Uzbek introduces pronounced computational bottlenecks in syntactic reordering, verbal morphology, and polysemous case-marker mapping. Utilizing standard automatic evaluation metrics—namely BLEU, chrF++, and METEOR—alongside structured human qualitative error classification (Multidimensional Quality Metrics - MQM), this study assesses automated translations across diverse registers, including news discourse, scientific prose, and legal texts.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Knowledge Integration and Cross-Model Knowledge Integration for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess substantial internal knowledge, yet their knowledge may be incomplete, inconsistent, outdated, or insufficiently coordinated across different tasks. Although existing research has investigated self-knowledge distillation, multi-model knowledge fusion, collaborative learning, and adaptive knowledge aggregation, these approaches do not necessarily provide a unified mechanism that dynamically switches between self-knowledge integration and cross-model knowledge integration according to the evolving knowledge requirements of multiple LLMs. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Knowledge Integration and Cross-Model Knowledge Integration (ASCI), a conceptual framework designed to coordinate these two complementary knowledge-processing modes. In self-knowledge integration, an individual LLM consolidates, reorganizes, verifies, and reconciles knowledge available within its own knowledge resources. In cross-model knowledge integration, multiple LLMs exchange candidate knowledge, identify complementary information, resolve contradictions, and construct a more comprehensive shared knowledge representation. A knowledge-state assessment mechanism estimates uncertainty, knowledge gaps, contradiction levels, source reliability, and expected integration benefits. A switching controller uses these signals to select self-knowledge integration, cross-model knowledge integration, or a hybrid mode. The framework further introduces provenance-aware knowledge records, contradiction-sensitive aggregation, feedback-driven switching, and safeguards against redundant communication and negative knowledge transfer. Unlike a permanently isolated model or a permanently collaborative multi-model system, ASCI treats the choice of knowledge-integration mode as a dynamic decision. This paper formalizes the framework, describes its algorithmic workflow, establishes research hypotheses, and proposes an experimental protocol for evaluating its effectiveness. Because the framework has not yet been experimentally validated in this paper, its potential benefits are presented as hypotheses rather than established empirical findings.

title: Design and Implementation of Personalized Learning Paths for College English Under the Drive of Digital Intelligence Technology
abstract: This case study examines a personalized learning system in a College English course at a Chinese university. Facing diverse proficiency and low engagement, the teaching team adopted a digital intelligence platform using learner profiling, adaptive recommendations, and real-time feedback. Content was adjusted based on student performance and behavior. Over one semester, an experimental class (n=60) using the system was compared with a control group (n=60) using traditional methods. Results showed improved learning outcomes, higher task completion, and increased satisfaction in the experimental group. Challenges included initial student resistance, increased teacher workload during setup, and data privacy concerns. Faculty needed training to interpret data while maintaining pedagogical control. It offers practical lessons for integrating AI-driven personalization in higher education, especially in language teaching, emphasizing benefits and managerial considerations for sustainable implementation.

title: DeepLNM: A Multimodal Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Accurate assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for prognostic stratification and treatment selection in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet imaging and routine pathology can yield false-negative/false-positive results. We propose DeepLNM, a multi-center foundation model for LNM prediction in CRC, evaluated with retrospective, external, prospective, and user study evidence. A multimodal dataset was assembled from three hospitals, with matched hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSI), CT scans, and text. DeepLNM achieved a mean AUC of 0.922 in the internal cohort and AUCs of 0.872 and 0.848 in two external cohorts. In a prospective cohort from a registered clinical trial (NCT07239063), DeepLNM remained robust (AUC = 0.845). In a user study, DeepLNM improved diagnostic accuracy, especially for junior pathologists (95.0%-97.3%), while reducing diagnostic time and increasing confidence. To explore the model's generalizability, it was further validated in a gastric cancer cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.793. Finally, DeepLNM identified histopathological features associated with LNM, addressing the "black-box" concern of deep learning. Together, these results position DeepLNM as a clinically preliminarily validated multimodal model for predicting LNM status in CRC, potentially facilitating the clinical translation of AI pathology.

title: Forecast lead time and the timing of crew deployment for weather-driven power outages using AI weather models
abstract: Utilities request mutual aid crews to restore power after severe storms, and requesting early secures more crews but relies on less accurate forecasts. We examined how forecast lead time affects the value of outage predictions for crew deployment, using operational forecasts from two AI weather models, GraphCast and FourCastNet, to predict outage occurrence for counties across the contiguous United States 24 to 120 hours ahead. Forecasts were evaluated by the share of outage burden captured by the counties where crews would be staged. Captured burden declined with lead time: the loss between three and five days was significant in all analyses, whereas the loss within three days was significant only for outages that had not yet started. Early deployment with all requested crews outperformed late deployment with fewer, and we report the availability ratio at which the two break even. Antecedent land surface predictors computed at forecast valid time include weather from the forecast period, which inflates their skill by 42 to 53% and reverses their apparent advantage over forecast meteorology at long lead times. Computed correctly, they improved occurrence skill by 17.5% at 24 hours but did not significantly change captured burden, a gap that attribution analysis linked to their static component. Prediction intervals covered only 0.476 of tropical cyclone events against a nominal 0.90. Calibration by hazard class corrected most of this shortfall at an 11% cost in interval width, as a diagnostic only, because hazard class is known only after the event.

title: Beyond Reachability: A Relation-Semantic Reasoning Framework for Biomedical Multi-hop QA
abstract: Biomedical multi-hop reasoning over knowledge graphs requires identifying a semantically valid relation sequence that supports the answer. Existing methods can retrieve correct answers, yet often rank them poorly within a large pool of seemingly relevant candidates. Even when a correct answer is retrieved, its associated evidence and reasoning path may fail to support the relation composition required by the question. We term this disconnect between answer reachability and evidential validity the reachable-but-invalid problem. We present ReSemReason, which shares a question-induced distribution over typed, directed relation schemas between candidate discovery and evidence selection. Schema compatibility guides graph search; ReSemAttn then uses relation-conditioned key/value projections and an uncertainty-weighted path prior to attend to candidate-specific evidence. A separate absolute-support score complements normalized attention when all retrieved paths are weak. The reported experiments on BioHopR, PrimeKGQA, and MedReason show improvements in answer ranking and answer-set quality. Path-discrimination analyses examine the distinction between endpoint correctness and evidential support. We also specify matched controls for search, attention, and schema uncertainty.

title: RDCompGS: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting with Image Codecs
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis but requires significant storage and transmission resources. Mapping Gaussian attributes to 2D representations enables efficient compression using mature image codecs. However, Gaussian representations that achieve comparable rendering quality are generally treated similarly during optimization, despite substantial differences in coding rate, leading to limited rate-distortion (R-D) performance after compression. To address this limitation, we propose RDCompGS, a 3DGS compression method that enables overall R-D optimization of Gaussian representations with respect to subsequent coding. A differentiable estimate of the coding rate is incorporated into the R-D optimization with rendering distortion. The rate constraint adjustment model further regulates the R-D trade-off across different compression conditions. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that RDCompGS achieves average Bjøntegaard Delta Rate reductions of 37.84% and 49.31% with H.265/HEVC and JPEG XL, respectively. The estimated rate also shows a strong correlation with the actual bit-rate under different compression conditions.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy Model and Information Loss Minimization for Protecting User Medical and Nutritional Data
abstract: This paper develops an adaptive differential privacy model and a stochastic information loss minimization method for protecting multi-parameter medical and nutritional data streams in digital healthcare systems. The latent correlation between clinical indicators and dietary attributes is quantified via Shannon entropy and mutual information to derive attribute criticality weights. To prevent premature privacy budget exhaustion during continuous monitoring, a six-step sliding-window budget allocation model is constructed. Furthermore, an analytical cube-root budget allocation rule is derived using Lagrange multipliers, coupled with a physiological state-space Kalman post-processing filter to reconstruct noisy time series without violating differential privacy guarantees. Experimental evaluations confirm a 63.3–64.6% reduction in relative squared information loss compared to uniform budget allocation while preserving clinical utility.

title: Data-Driven Sparse Reconstruction Framework for Anomaly Detection in Smart Manufacturing Environment
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection of sensor measurements is essential for monitoring complex systems in smart manufacturing environments. However, conventional approaches often require predefined statistical assumptions or explicit knowledge of physical measurement models. Therefore, a data-driven sparse reconstruction framework (DSRF) is proposed for anomaly detection without requiring explicit noise distribution or separate identification of a physical measurement model. The proposed framework decomposes observation deviations into a reconstructed normal measurement component, a sparse anomaly residual, and a remaining reconstruction residual. The DSRF is evaluated using current and vibration measurements from robot welding systems. Normal measurements are divided into training, validation, and independent test subsets, while labeled abnormal samples are reserved for final evaluation. Training data are used to learn an effective sensing matrix and determine anomaly thresholds. At the 99th-percentile threshold, DSRF achieves 100% detection with no false negatives and accuracies of 99.76% and 98.38% for the current and vibration datasets, respectively. Comparative experiments with PCA reconstruction and an autoencoder show similarly high classification performance while DSRF only provides a larger threshold-normalized separation and explicitly estimates sparse anomaly residuals. The anomaly residual also provides frequency feature-level information for interpreting prominent abnormal deviations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of DSRF for anomaly detection and residual-based interpretation without explicit noise assumptions or separately identified physical system models.

title: Improving geochemical anomaly recognition associated with mineralization via counterfactual causal inference
abstract: Identifying geochemical anomalies in lithologically complex regions remains challenging due to the superposition of multiple geological processes, which complicates the separation of regional background from mineralization-related signals. Here, we propose a counterfactual-inspired framework that reframes an anomaly as the deviation of an observed value from its expected background under a non-mineralization scenario, thereby extending conventional unsupervised outlier detection approaches by incorporating spatial prior information from known mineral occurrences. This framework integrates three stages: (1) median quantile regression forest (QRF-M) to isolate a clean background, (2) causal forest to quantify spatial association with known mineral occurrences, and (3) extraction of counterfactual anomalies by predicting background concentrations exclusively from non-mineralized areas. The method yielded three main findings. First, QRF-M suppresses outliers, producing unbiased regional geochemical background estimates, and identifies Fe 2 O 3 , SiO 2 , and Ti as primary background controls. Second, the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT = 12.08 ppm) exceeds the average treatment effect (ATE = 3.02 ppm), suggesting spatially heterogeneous enrichment near known deposits. Third, the counterfactual method achieves an anomaly recognition rate of 73.7 % within 5 km of known occurrences—higher than conventional threshold (47.7 %) and QRF-M (50.5 %) methods—while reducing false anomalies and highlighting three prospective areas not flagged by comparison methods. However, because the same known occurrences are used both to define the treatment variable and to evaluate spatial coincidence, this efficiency index is subject to dual-use evaluation bias and should be regarded as a retrospective brownfield benchmark for well-explored brownfield settings, not as an independent prospective validation or evidence of universal algorithmic superiority. Its primary value lies in detecting weak mineralization signals in low-background areas that conventional methods often miss, though the highlighted targets require field verification.

title: Decision-FLIP: Budget-Free Structured Pruning for Gaussian Occupancy Models
abstract: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. Common pruning proxies, such as opacity, activation frequency, or parameter magnitude, do not measure whether removing a row changes the model's voxel decisions. We introduce Decision-FLIP, a budget-free compilation framework whose scoring and structure selection need only unlabeled calibration inputs. Exact Mean-FLIP scores each persistent row by the number of voxel argmax decisions that change when the row is removed from the readout; a guarded Otsu split of the log-score distribution selects the survivor count without a target and abstains when the split is unsupported; and the survivors are physically compiled into a smaller checkpoint, so camera sampling, attention, and aggregation shrink with the bank. For streaming banks, scores are integrated over each row's lifecycle through warp, death, and refill. Across four Gaussian-bank model-dataset settings and one persistent-query transfer, the automatically selected cuts remove 12-79% of eligible rows and cut bank/query-dependent latency by 7-45% across settings with component profiles, with whole-model savings of up to 8.0% on the primary endpoints bounded by fixed-cost image, voxel, and sensor modules and peak-memory savings of up to 16.6%. Under matched one-epoch recovery controls, semantic mIoU changes by at most 0.18 point. Same-$K$ controls show that the ranking, not only the bank size, matters: random removal collapses GaussianFormer-1 and OccFormer, while label-free Mean-FLIP matches or outperforms supervised Taylor ranking on all five settings where that control was run. The method applies when removable primitives keep a stable checkpoint-row identity; it is budget-free in survivor count, not parameter-free.

title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design
abstract: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

title: Discriminative Score Function: Turning Pretrained Models into Functional Generative Priors
abstract: Discriminative models are trained with task-specific objectives such as classification, detection, or representation learning, yet their practical utility depends on generalizing beyond the training task to unseen samples from the same domain. This suggests that a discriminative model may retain an implicit trace of the data manifold beyond its task labels. We ask whether this trace can be exposed as a generative signal without task-specific guidance. We introduce the Discriminative Score Function (DSF), which extracts an image-space generative field from the loss-gradient geometry of a pretrained discriminative model. DSF provides a training-free update rule that moves images toward model-consistent visual regions without retraining or task-specific targets. We apply DSF to diverse pretrained discriminative models, including ResNet classifiers, DETR detectors, and DINOv2 ViT encoders. DSF generates unconditional images from noise and supports conditional guidance, editing, inpainting, and explanation through the same field. DSF-generated samples also provide effective zero-shot quantization calibration when real images or labels are unavailable, preserving feature geometry better than data-free calibration baselines. These results show that discriminative training leaves a generative functional signal for synthesis and calibration. Project page: https://junhoo.me/dsf.

title: Heuristica Neuronal
abstract: Este documento presenta CerebroTotal, una arquitectura computacional basada en la heurística neuronal real del cerebro humano, diseñada para operar con complejidad O(1) y reproducir los mecanismos de difusión, resonancia, inhibición y emergencia que caracterizan el pensamiento humano. El sistema implementa memoria sin duplicados, filtrado automático de ruido, narración emergente por trigrams y aprendizaje en tiempo real sin reentrenamiento. Se demuestra empíricamente que el pulso heurístico mantiene tiempo constante incluso cuando la red crece más de 600 veces, superando estructuralmente a los modelos estadísticos como los LLM, cuya atención es O(n²). El paper incluye comparativas reales, pruebas matemáticas, resultados de diagnóstico, reconocimiento de patrones y análisis de eficiencia, mostrando que CerebroTotal logra capacidades narrativas y de razonamiento con cientos de palabras aprendidas, manteniendo ventajas que los LLM no pueden obtener por diseño: operación offline, costo cero, transparencia total y determinismo exacto. Es una propuesta de arquitectura alternativa inspirada directamente en la neurociencia y optimizada para eficiencia extrema.

title: Sistema Criptográfico No Invertible con Claves Fantasma Resistencia Total a Ataques Clásicos y Cuánticos
abstract: Este documento presenta un sistema criptográfico basado en una operación matemática no invertible que genera múltiples soluciones válidas llamadas claves fantasma. Estas claves producen exactamente la misma firma que la clave real, haciendo imposible distinguir la verdadera entre las falsas. El paper explica por qué el sistema es resistente a ataques clásicos y cuánticos, detalla el comportamiento multisolución, muestra un ejemplo real con 1960 claves fantasma y demuestra mediante código Python la imposibilidad de recuperar la clave real. La seguridad depende exclusivamente de evitar errores humanos externos al mecanismo matemático.

title: Prompt Complexity, Overprompting, and the Honesty of Error in LLM-Based Mechanical Drawing Interpretation: A Structured Empirical Evaluation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret mechanical engineering drawings, yet the main risk is a wrong answer that reads as correct. We report an exploratory empirical study of how prompt design and evaluation shape the reliability of this interpretation, in two connected stages over the same twenty drawings. Stage 1 runs one prose prompting protocol on two model families and finds that progressive enrichment does not improve accuracy; beyond a threshold, it raises confident fabrication. Stage 2 compares six structured prompt architectures at thirty repetitions per cell, producing 3540 generations scored under four judge conditions. Across both stages, identification accuracy does not improve, while the rate of claims the drawing does not support varies by nearly an order of magnitude with prompt architecture. Only a judge that sees the drawing can measure it; a text-only judge inflates confident fabrication three to four times, making evaluator modality a first-order variable. Without a ground-truth answer, an image-only check can test only whether claims are visible; it recovers about half of the reference flags, enough for human-in-the-loop triage. A judge from another model family reproduces the ranking. We distill five practical recommendations for this setting.

title: HT-Net: A Task-Specific Dual-Branch Network for Tumor Segmentation in Histopathological Images
abstract: Breast cancer, the most prevalent malignancy among women globally, requires precise assessment of lymph node metastases in whole-slide images (WSIs) for accurate clinical staging and therapeutic planning. However, manual assessment is laborious and prone to inter-observer variability. Inspired by biomimetic principles of functional specialization and complementary visual perception, we propose Head–Tail Network (HT-Net), a novel dual-branch encoder network for histopathological image segmentation. HT-Net employs a HeadBranch with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention to prioritize background feature selection and a TailBranch with a novel Hybrid Multi-Scale Attention (HMSA) module to resolve complex tumor boundaries. Features from both branches are integrated through a spatially adaptive fusion module and reconstructed using a U-Net-style decoder. A task-specific supervision loss further enforces functional specialization between branches and mitigates class imbalance. Experiments demonstrate that HT-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, UCTransNet, VM-UNet, and nnWNet. On Camelyon16, HT-Net achieved 89.37% mDice and 82.05% mIoU, surpassing nnWNet by 0.86 and 1.08 percentage points, respectively. On Glas, it achieved 93.04% mDice and 86.95% mIoU, exceeding nnWNet by 0.30 and 0.47 percentage points. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the biomimetic-inspired functional specialization strategy for automated histopathological image segmentation.

title: Privacy Preservation and Optimisation of Electric Vehicles
abstract: This thesis develops practical ways to protect sensitive information generated by electric vehicles and their charging stations. Such information can reveal users’ travel patterns, charging behaviour, vehicle status and locations, creating risks of surveillance, misuse and cyberattacks. The research develops privacy protection methods that adapt to changing data, protect information when many requests occur at the same time, and maintain accurate energy demand predictions. These methods aim to balance privacy with data accuracy, helping build safer and more trustworthy electric vehicle and charging infrastructure. The research can support secure transportation, efficient energy management and wider adoption of electric vehicles.

title: A Calculus of Execution for Systems of Interacting Binary Relations: Constitutive Admissibility Without a Choice Selector
abstract: As AI-enabled software becomes agentic and evolutive, we formulate a structural sufficiency condition and two execution-level requirements for accountable evolution: fixed-regime execution must remain within a standard Borel representation closed under finite/countable products required by local execution and path construction (S0); governing changes must be executable within the same apparatus they govern (R1); and every admitted act must remain deterministically verifiable from the context and governing specification under which it was admitted (R2). We develop a calculus for interacting executable binary relations. Execution uses an asymmetric epistemic–ontological–eschatological (OEE) structure: an append-only context records admitted events; a partial single-valued realization yields at most one candidate per invocation; a Boolean criterion decides admission; and fixed Axiom 0 records admissible realizations. Standard Borel product closure provides the measurable carrier for local execution, while repeated Axiom 0 defines Eschatological Induction; Zermelo–Fraenkel coding separately enforces rank discipline. Under stated assumptions, we discharge S0, establish common admission semantics for governance and operation under OEE closure, and obtain deterministic verification replay. The fixed-regime path space has a countable/perfect dichotomy. Axiom 0 invokes no global choice selector; that problem appears only after projection to the coordinate-free relational reduct. Fixed-point and recursive-descent results require separate monotonicity and well-foundedness assumptions.

title: Resolution Allocation with Learnable Resizing and Spectral Filter Parameterization
abstract: Learnable downsampling and spectral-domain filter parameterizations have each made convolutional networks more flexible, but their interaction has not been systematically examined. We bridge this gap by examining convolutional kernels learned in the spatial and spectral domains, together with learned downsampling ratios under a cropped resizing implementation. We find that spectral and spatial kernels respond differently to learned resolution allocation, with larger gains for the spectral kernel. We observe this consistently on three datasets (EuroSAT, CIFAR-10 and STL-10) and at two model sizes (differences in accuracy gain of +0.013 to +0.028 on held-out test sets). Part of this difference reflects the greater gain of the spectral kernel from retaining more spatial area, but the difference remains positive when total retained area is matched. This pattern is observed across datasets and model sizes, although its magnitude and dependence on the complexity budget vary with model size and the resizing implementation.

title: HyperLoop: Hyperspectral-Assisted Loop Closure Detection in 3D-SLAM for Planetary Exploration
abstract: Autonomous navigation of planetary rovers is challenged by visually repetitive, featureless terrain. SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offer dense mapping but rely on RGB appearance descriptors that degrade under perceptual aliasing - a common failure mode in extraterrestrial environments where physically distinct locations appear visually identical. This paper presents HyperLoop, the first framework integrating hyperspectral imaging (HSI) into the loop closure module of a 3DGS-based SLAM system. Hyperspectral descriptors encode material-level spectral signatures complementing RGB features, providing robustness to illumination changes and visual repetitiveness. Two HSI descriptor families are introduced: Bag-of-Spectral-Words (BoSW), encoding spectral material distributions via TF-IDF weighted histograms, and PCA-K VLAD (PCAK-VLAD), capturing first-order residual statistics of PCA-compressed spectral signatures. Both are evaluated with SIFT-VLAD and NetVLAD RGB descriptors under Strict-AND and Weighted fusion strategies on a custom dataset from the Moon-Mars Outdoor Test Site (MMOTS) at DLR, comprising synchronized RGB-D and hyperspectral sequences across four planetary analog traverses (65.5 m total). A key finding is that the sensor's Red-NIR range (600-860 nm) provides limited discriminability for rock terrain: the best HSI fusion (SIFT-VLAD + BoSW, Strict-AND) achieves 5.04 cm ATE RMSE, within 1.8% of SIFT-VLAD alone (4.95 cm). The gain over NetVLAD (8.81 cm) is attributable to SIFT-VLAD, not HSI fusion. This motivates future adoption of SWIR sensors capturing diagnostic mineral absorption features absent from the 600-860 nm range for planetary SLAM missions.

title: Opportunities and limitations of using generative artificial intelligence in the development of a minimum viable product for non-technical founders
abstract: Ustanovitelj brez tehničnega znanja se pri prvem digitalnem produktu sooča s tehničnimi, kompetenčnimi, časovnimi in finančnimi omejitvami hkrati, tehnično sposobnost pa lahko pridobi le prek tehničnega soustanovitelja, zunanjega izvajalca ali lastnega učenja programiranja, pri čemer ima vsaka pot svojo ceno. Orodja generativne umetne inteligence odpirajo četrti kanal do te sposobnosti, odprto pa ostaja vprašanje, koliko ta dostop stane in kje se izčrpa. Delo obravnava razvoj preproste rezervacijske aplikacije za manjše storitveno podjetje po dveh poteh: prek razvojne agencije ter samostojno z orodji Lovable, Bolt in Claude Code. Poti sta primerjani po sedmih merilih, med njimi po stroških, času, potrebnih kompetencah, kakovosti in odvisnosti od platforme. Razlika je največja pri neposrednih denarnih stroških. Agencijski razvoj je ocenjen na približno 4.563 do 5.625 USD za 73 do 75 ur dela , samostojni razvoj pa na 25 USD mesečno pri Lovable ali Boltu oziroma 38 do 41 USD pri Claude Code , ob 40 do 50 urah lastnega dela ustanovitelja, kar je razpon med orodji in ne enotna vrednost. Orodja zadostujejo pri vidnih in strukturno preprostejših nalogah, pri poslovni logiki, varnosti, zunanjih povezavah in nevidnem delu pa je njihova zadostnost pogojna. Ugotovitve kažejo, da tehnične omejitve ostanejo, le pokažejo se drugje: cenejši začetek razvoja prinese prenos odgovornosti za preverjanje in varnost na ustanovitelja, ki rezultata pogosto ne zna ustrezno presoditi.

title: Sociolinguistic Equivalence in Multilingual Language Model Evaluation: Reproducibility Supplement
abstract: Reproducibility Supplement for “Sociolinguistic Equivalence in Multilingual Language Model Evaluation” This supplementary software package supports the position paper Sociolinguistic Equivalence in Multilingual Language Model Evaluation by Irene Theodoropoulou. It provides a dependency-free Python implementation of the proposed finite-state sociolinguistic-equivalence discrepancy, based on optimal transport with a prespecified warranted response relation. The package includes: Python source code for computing the discrepancy. Automated unit tests verifying the mathematical properties and analytical examples. A constructed Greek–English example illustrating protected task commitments, warranted linguistic adaptation, and response compatibility. A README explaining installation-free execution and reproducibility. All numerical examples use hypothetical distributions. No large language model experiments were conducted to generate these examples, and the package contains no private datasets, consumer-service outputs, or proprietary API dependencies. The materials are intended to support computational transparency, reproducibility, and future research on sociolinguistically informed evaluation of multilingual language models. Related manuscript: Sociolinguistic Equivalence in Multilingual Language Model Evaluation (Position Paper submitted or intended for submission to Computational Linguistics). Author: Irene Theodoropoulou, Deree, The American University of Greece.

title: Information Coarse-Graining O: Verification Layer—Solvable Model Locking and Pre-Registered Adjudication Execution of the Information-Conditioning Coefficient
abstract: A theoretical program whose main body consists of conditional theorems concentrates its quantitative content in a small number of functions; before the functionalforms are locked, all theorems exist in conditional form. This paper executes thepre-registered machine-check protocol for the pivotal quantity of the program—theinformation-conditioning coefficient—and fixes the adjudication criteria for everynumerical conclusion in the form of adjudication windows before data generation.The execution environment is: fixed aggregation scheme, fixed quotient readoutconvention, and logarithmic scale domain restricted by the pre-declared saturationupper bound and the fine-scale isolation protocol. All numerical values are generated by a single computational pipeline. The main results are as follows. First, theconditioning-coefficient curve of the parameterized tree baseline exhibits constantbehavior across four independent weight realizations, the confidence interval of thelinear-fit slope crosses zero, and the regime-discrimination adjudication is the extensive regime; at the same time, the anchor adjudication window is adjudicatedas failed according to the registered criterion, and the anchor is downgraded to aparameter-point case—this downgrade itself constitutes the first empirical demonstration of adjudication independence. title: Replicable Dueling Bandits
abstract: Dueling bandits choose each comparison based on earlier noisy outcomes, so two runs on the same preferences can compare different pairs. We study replicable dueling bandits, where two executions with shared internal randomness and independent comparison outcomes must select the same ordered pair in every round with probability at least $1-ρ$. Building on Beat-the-Mean, whose scores change as arms are eliminated and need not rank the best arm highest, we design the first such algorithms with sublinear regret. Under relaxed stochastic transitivity with parameter $γ\ge 1$ and the stochastic triangle inequality, we design an algorithm that achieves expected regret $\widetilde{O}(γ^8 K^4 H_{\mathrm{p}}/ρ^2)$, where $H_{\mathrm{p}}=\sum_{i=2}^{K}(P_{1i}-1/2)^{-1}$. Under strong stochastic transitivity, we design an algorithm based on simultaneous elimination that improves the dependence on $K$ and achieves $\widetilde{O}(K^2 H_{\mathrm{p}}/ρ^2)$ regret. For linear dueling bandits, we design an algorithm that achieves regret $\widetilde{O}(d^3\sqrt{T}/(c_μρ))$. Experiments on synthetic and language-model preferences show replicability, with sublinear regret.

title: Value-Informed Schedule Trimming for Accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo Guidance in Discrete Diffusion
abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Active guidance steps require additional reward evaluations and, for gradient-based proposals, value-gradient computations. Sparse guidance reduces this cost by guiding only a subset of timesteps, but commonly used schedules are fixed heuristics whose effectiveness can vary substantially across tasks. We propose VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects guided timesteps under a fixed budget. VISTA formulates sparse guidance as approximation of the ideal full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable upper bound on \(\ell_1\) path deviation. Using value statistics collected from a small number of full-guidance warmup generations, VISTA optimizes the resulting empirical surrogate exactly via dynamic programming. The warmup generations can be retained as model outputs, and after schedule selection VISTA has the same per-generation guidance complexity as other sparse schedules with the same budget. Across text, biological sequence, and image generation tasks, VISTA discovers task-dependent schedules and outperforms hand-designed sparse schedules in most tested settings, while approaching or exceeding full-guidance performance on several task metrics. In toxic-text generation, for example, VISTA attains a 0.99 unique-toxic ratio compared with 1.00 for full guidance while reducing post-selection per-generation latency from 204.23 s to 38.16 s, a 5.35$\times$ speedup.

title: Reducing the Gap Between Spatial and Space-Filling Curve Neighbors in 3D Point Cloud Segmentation
abstract: As a lightweight and highly accurate method for nearest-neighbor search in 3D point clouds, approaches based on space-filling curves (SFC) have been proposed. However, due to the inherent properties of SFC, a gap arises between proximity relationships along the SFC and those in the original Euclidean space. In this study, we propose a loss function that reduces the influence of this gap. Specifically, we compute the distances between adjacent points along the SFC and train the model to optimize feature similarity between pairs of points that are distant from each other in the original 3D space. We incorporate the proposed method into a high-performing 3D point cloud segmentation model and evaluate its effectiveness on three datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods on both indoor and outdoor point cloud datasets.

title: AURELIANO - A Human–AI Hybrid Operational Framework for Decision Intelligence Context Management and Human
abstract: The increasing availability of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems has expanded the possibilities for developing personalized, context-sensitive forms of human–AI collaboration. The effectiveness of such collaborations depends not only on the capabilities of the underlying language model but also on the organization of interaction, the management of contextual information, the consistency of operational rules, the verification of outputs and the allocation of decision-making authority. This paper presents Aureliano, an experimental Human–AI Hybrid Hub (HAHH) framework designed to structure these dimensions within an existing generative AI environment. Rather than introducing a new foundational model, Aureliano operates as a higher-level cognitive and procedural framework that organizes the interaction between a human principal and a general-purpose AI system. Its central objectives are to improve contextual continuity, mitigate semantic drift and entropy, distinguish evidence from inference, support complex reasoning, maintain decision traceability and preserve human authority over consequential decisions. The framework is examined through a conceptual architecture, an operational state-management model, a structured epistemic classification scheme, a human-in-the-loop validation mechanism and an exploratory verification approach. Particular attention is devoted to the distinction between persistent information and autonomous memory, between behavioral consistency and model identity and between internally reported test results and independently reproducible empirical evidence. The analysis suggests that a substantial part of the practical value of personalized AI collaboration may be produced by the systematic organization of the human–AI interface rather than by modifications to the underlying model. Nevertheless, this proposition requires controlled empirical evaluation. The paper therefore distinguishes the framework's specified properties, reported experimental observations and unresolved hypotheses. The contribution is a transferable conceptual approach to the design and evaluation of human-controlled, context-aware AI collaboration, with implications for decision support, knowledge management, organizational analysis and responsible AI governance.

title: Is learning difficulty just missing prerequisites?
abstract: A short conjecture note proposing that, with an appropriate decomposition of knowledge, every elementary learning unit has the same expected acquisition cost once its prerequisites are mastered. It discusses the limits of an existing learning system, the risk of a circular definition of ideal decomposition, and a possible empirical test. The conjecture is unproven. The conjecture is mine. AI helped turn it into words.

title: The Symbolactuality Paradox (SAP)
abstract: AbstractThe Symbolactuality Paradox (SAP) proposes a candidate domain-independent systemic principle concerning situations in which a system produces a symbolic, linguistic, representational, or otherwise surface-level marker associated with an intended outcome without thereby realizing the corresponding functional state. The originating case is an instructional interaction in which an intended diagram insertion is represented by an output such as a placement label or completion marker rather than by the functional realization of the requested diagram.The central distinction is therefore not between artificial and human systems, nor between one particular task and another, but between representation and realization. The candidate mechanism is expressed asRequirement → Symbolic/Representational Completion \neq Functional Realization.The associated apparent-completion relation isApparent Completion \neq Actual Completion.The paper develops a three-layer architecture. The first layer preserves the originating case at the philosophical-epistemological level. The second translates the distinction into systemic and cybernetic variables. The third constructs an operational mathematical framework in which criterion-specific divergence between representation and realization can be measured. A general system state is represented by t, with discrete dynamics t+1 = F(t, u, \theta) or continuous dynamics \dot{t} = F(t, u, t, \theta). The principal candidate observable is \Delta_{SA} = D_{C}(R(C, M, I), F(C, M, I)).The framework is explicitly presented as a candidate principle rather than as an established universal law. Its empirical status depends on operationalization, preregistered predictions where appropriate, counterexample testing, synthetic simulation, and cross-domain validation. The manuscript provides a 38-case validation architecture, while distinguishing documented observations from synthetic illustrative data. The mathematical formulation is intended to function as a measurement and testing architecture rather than as decorative formalism.

title: Initial and final keyword lists
abstract: The final set of publications was then scanned for mentions of technologies in order to establish a baseline collection of technology keywords. Again, the corpus was too large to complete examine manually, so the Mistral LLM was used to search for mentions of technologies. The LLM was given the title and abstract of each publication in the corpus in turn with instructions to “extract any technologies mentioned in those papers” (full system prompt in section A.1). For the purposes of this analysis, I considered a technology to be any of: programming languages, software tools/libraries, hardware or hardware platforms, and named conceptual or algorithmic frameworks the authors applied as part of their method. I took a broad stance for the definition of technology with the dual intention of a) not eliminating anything that could be useful for further analysis and b) being able to manually review and cull the list generated by the LLM. The 17,476 results returned by the LLM did feature a large number of duplicates, either as explicit duplicates, or as ontological duplicates or subsumption redundancies; as well as spurious entries arising as either a misidentification of a technology by the LLM or from publications that passed the previous filter step but were not dealing with automated assessment of training and education. I used the Python’s rapidfuzz with a conservative similarity setting of 90% and regular expressions libraries to condense duplicates and near duplicates (plurals, acronyms, and highly similar words) into single entries, resulting in 11,560 technology keywords. I then culled spurious entries by removing all items with less than 20 mentions across the corpus, reducing 11,560 keywords to 1,907. With the keyword list now tractable for human review, I then manually removed any keywords unrelated to automated assessment or too broad to be useful, resulting in a final list of 455 technology keywords relevant to automated assessment.The final step was to flatten subsumption redundancies and create a taxonomy that mapped the keywords to a useful classification system for analysis. I used a set of mutually exclusive hierarchical categories with a most-specific-level coding rule (assigning each item to the most specific category it qualifies for, falling back to a broader/residual category if no finer one applies) with NEC (Not Elsewhere Classified) residual categories at each level of generality, to code the 458 technology keywords into 13 categories deemed useful for our analysis: LLM, Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Rules-Based Systems, Statistical Assessment Tools, Educational Data Mining, Blockchain, Intelligent Tutoring Systems, Massive Open Online Course, Multiple Choice Questions, and General Automated Assessment Concepts.

title: Data Structures in Python
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive introduction to Python’s core data structures, focusing on their creation, manipulation, and practical applications. It begins with lists, versatile and mutable data types that support operations like indexing, slicing, appending, reversing, and sorting. This chapter demonstrates these through clear examples, such as list comprehensions for filtering and transforming data (e.g., generating cubes or filtering positive/negative numbers), and highlights common pitfalls like mismatched variable assignments during unpacking. It also introduces the split() function for string-to-list conversion and the Counter class for word frequency analysis, emphasizing Python’s flexibility in handling heterogeneous data. This chapter progresses to vectors and matrices, illustrating vector operations such as addition, subtraction, dot products, and matrix manipulation through nested loops for initialization and computation. Queues are introduced as FIFO structures, with examples using the deque class, while tuples are presented as immutable lists, showcasing their creation and limitations. Sets are explored for their ability to handle unique elements and support set-theoretic operations like union and intersection, with efficient O(1) lookup. Dictionaries, as key-value hash tables, are covered extensively, including creation, iteration, and methods like get() and items(), with advanced features like OrderedDict for maintaining insertion order and defaultdict for complex data structures. This chapter concludes with a brief exploration of functional programming concepts, such as user-defined functions with *args and **kwargs for flexible argument handling, and serialization using the pickle module for data persistence. It also distinguishes between mutable (lists, dictionaries, sets) and immutable (strings, tuples, integers) types, with examples like string concatenation to illustrate immutability constraints. Additional sequence types like bytearray and xrange are mentioned, alongside techniques like enumeration and sequence unpacking, providing a solid foundation for Python’s data manipulation capabilities. This chapter equips readers with practical skills for working with Python’s data structures, supported by clear code examples and error-handling insights. By covering both basic operations and advanced techniques like comprehensions and dictionary sorting, it prepares readers for deeper exploration in subsequent chapters, particularly in applying these structures to DeepSeek and other computational tasks.

title: Task-Centric Multimodal Learning for Cognitive Impairment Detection
abstract: Dementia affects millions of older adults worldwide, yet early detection remains difficult outside clinical settings. Traditional models primarily rely on text or voice-based responses, capturing only a limited view of human cognition despite the inherently multimodal nature of human expression. This work proposes a contactless, multimodal screening framework that leverages video, audio, and text signals collected during structured voice-based interactions with Amazon Alexa. By incorporating these modalities, our approach captures a more holistic representation of human behavior encompassing speech patterns, vocal characteristics, facial expressions, and linguistic structure, which may enable more accurate detection of cognitive decline. Different participants completed three conversational tasks designed to probe spontaneous speech, comprehension, and recall. We pursued three objectives: (1) evaluate which of the three Alexa tasks provides the most informative cognitive signals, (2) compare the effectiveness of unimodal models, and (3) assess the benefits of multimodal fusion models. Task-level analysis shows that the video model achieves its best performance on Command-Reading, with an accuracy of 0.65 (AUC 0.69), while the audio model performs best on Question-Answering, reaching an accuracy of 0.67 (AUC 0.73). In contrast, the multimodal model demonstrates consistently stable performance across tasks, achieving an accuracy of 0.76 (AUC 0.75) on Command-Reading and 0.76 (AUC 0.73) on Question-Answering. These findings demonstrate that multimodal behavioral cues captured through naturalistic interactions can reliably distinguish MCI from healthy aging, highlighting the limitations of traditional diagnostic paradigms and supporting the shift toward multimodal, real-world cognitive assessment frameworks.

Task-level analysis shows that the video model achieves its best performance on Command-Reading, with an accuracy of 0.65 (AUC 0.69), while the audio model performs best on Question-Answering, reaching an accuracy of 0.67 (AUC 0.73). In contrast, the multimodal model demonstrates consistently stable performance across tasks, achieving an accuracy of 0.76 (AUC 0.75) on Command-Reading and 0.76 (AUC 0.73) on Question-Answering. These findings demonstrate that multimodal behavioral cues captured through naturalistic interactions can reliably distinguish MCI from healthy aging, highlighting the limitations of traditional diagnostic paradigms and supporting the shift toward multimodal, real-world cognitive assessment frameworks.

title: Complementary Future Token Pruning for World Action Models
abstract: World action models (WAMs) jointly predict future visual states and robot actions, but processing dense future-frame tokens incurs substantial inference latency. We propose CF-Prune, a training-free framework for pruning future-frame tokens in pretrained WAMs. Our key insight is that future visual predictions support action generation and therefore need not preserve every visual detail required for high-fidelity video synthesis. CF-Prune combines instruction and action attention to identify task-relevant tokens during the initial denoising forward pass, even when future-frame and action representations remain highly noisy. An entropy-based phase identification mechanism further retains dense computation during precision phases to mitigate pruning-induced performance degradation. Experiments on RoboLab, RoboCasa, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate consistent inference speedups. At a 35% pruning ratio, CF-Prune achieves average speedups of 1.19-1.27x while improving task success rates. At a 50% pruning ratio, it achieves 1.29-1.33x average speedups on both simulation benchmarks, with overall success rates within 1.0 percentage point of the baseline.

title: ProtModernBERT: Compute-Efficient Protein Language Modeling
abstract: Large protein language models provide a powerful framework for learning sequence-function relationships and guiding experimental design. However, architectural improvements are underexplored, especially in low-compute regimes of relevance for resource-constrained research laboratories. We show that the training cost for encoder-only transformer architectures can be reduced by leveraging modern architectural refinements, offering an encouraging performance / compute-efficiency trade-off. We introduce ProtModernBERT, a modernized BERT-style model pre-trained on amino acid sequences, and compare it with ProtBert, Amplify, and ESM2 across a set of supervised structural tasks -encompassing secondary structure prediction, disorder prediction, and subcellular localization- and ProteinGym's zero-shot functional benchmark. We find that ProtModernBERT matches or closely tracks the performance of Amplify-120M and ProtBert with up to 80-90\% reduction in pre-training FLOPs, and narrows the gap to ESM2 when controlling for pre-training. Our analysis using a cluster-based validation protocol for hyperparameter selection and randomly initialized models disentangles the contributions of architecture and data, showing that modern components provide stronger inductive biases that are more consequential than parameter count in low-compute regimes.

title: Inteligencia artificial y marketing digital: reflexiones comparadas entre Colombia y panamá a partir del periplo internacional 2025
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) ha dejado de ser una herramienta emergente, para consolidarse como un motor central de innovación tecnológica en el marketing digital; a nivel global, este sector proyecta superar los 107.500 millones de dólares en 2028, con un crecimiento sostenido impulsado por algoritmos predictivos, automatización y personalización. Sin embargo, la adopción en América Latina presenta matices, en Colombia, cerca del 59 % de los consumidores interactúa cotidianamente con aplicaciones de IA, mientras que en Panamá el avance ha sido mayor debido a la inversión en infraestructura digital y políticas de innovación. Este ensayo analiza la relevancia de la IA en el marketing digital desde un enfoque comparativo, integrando cifras recientes, estudios de caso y reflexiones críticas; donde se plantea que, aunque la IA fortalece la personalización, la eficiencia y la optimización de campañas, su impacto depende de superar retos organizacionales, culturales y éticos.

title: EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos
abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstra- tions, yet transferring their manipulation priors to robot control remains chal- lenging. The commonly adopted retargeting-based approaches convert human wrist and finger poses into embodiment-specific action commands through hand- crafted geometric mappings. However, such mappings require meticulous recal- ibration across different embodiments and risk propagating hand-tracking errors into downstream robot control pipelines. To this end, we propose EgoJEPA, a three-stage framework that learns embodiment-agnostic representations from ego- centric human videos without rule-based human-to-robot retargeting: 1) Human- action pre-training learns effect-aware latent actions through JEPA-style visual prediction conditioned on hand-motion differences; 2) Latent-action-based world modeling jointly predicts future visual dynamics and latent actions, which decou- ples human prior pre-training from robot-specific control parameterizations; 3) Embodiment-specific tuning adapts the pretrained model to diverse robots through lightweight action adapters. Experiments on five real-world manipulation tasks across three robot embodiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of EgoJEPA. It achieves a 74% average success rate under the out-of-domain evalu- ation, compared with 65% for the retargeting baseline, while reducing cumulative cross-embodiment wall-clock cost by 47.2%, from 743.2 to 392.7 hours.

title: Sparse-QITE: Discovering Compact Generators for Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution via Regularization Methods
abstract: Quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE) provides a systematic route to ground-state preparation, but its cost grows rapidly with the locality $D$ of the unitary approximation, for which the local Pauli basis scales as $4^D$. We introduce Sparse-QITE, a regularized formulation that promotes compact generators, reducing the number of quantum operations and yielding circuits with fewer gates and lower depth. We derive rigorous bounds on the sparsification error and benchmark the method in one-dimensional transverse-field Ising and antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models. Sparse-QITE exhibits a controllable sparsity--accuracy trade-off while retaining strong compression even in the high-accuracy regime. In scalability experiments with respect to $D$, the active support grows much more slowly than in standard QITE and, in several regimes, approximately saturates over the domain sizes studied. After circuit construction and transpilation, some of the largest-domain cases require only about $1\%$ of the standard-QITE gate count while maintaining high accuracy. We further introduce adaptive and active-discovery variants: the former selects the regularization strength dynamically during the evolution, while the latter reduces the number of Pauli expectation values that need to be evaluated and, consequently, the measurement requirements. These results establish sparsity-promoting regularization as a route toward more resource-efficient QITE. More broadly, these results suggest that sparsity-promoting regularization may also benefit variational quantum algorithms.

title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

title: Trading energy for coherence in mode discrimination
abstract: Energy is arguably the main resource in classical physics; coherence is the prototypical quantum resource. In this paper, we study the interplay between these two resources in the task of optimal mode discrimination. This task, motivated by cryptography and metrology, consists of finding in which mode a signal has been encoded, for a given finite set of possible modes. After recalling that the task can be cast as a semi-definite program, we solve completely the case of two-mode discrimination under a hard energy constraint $n\leq N$. Specifically, we identify the region of modes overlap, for which the maximal energy state (the Fock state with N excitations) is the best choice for discrimination. For other overlaps, having access to coherence leads to better discrimination.

title: MakSafe: A Spatiotemporal Semantic Framework for Formal Specification and Compliance Checking of Road Vehicle Safety Rules
abstract: Scenario-based validation is essential for automated road vehicles but cannot cover the full variability of openworld traffic. We present MakSafe, a formal spatiotemporal framework for specifying and checking road vehicle safety rules through semantic zones, action-based forecasting, and trace-tree reasoning, avoiding uniform time discretization. We formalize the road network, vehicle states, and occupancy zones, then build executable rules for front-vehicle identification and timeto-collision (TTC) verification. The evaluation combines a tracedependent case study with a scalability benchmark over traffic density (N ), horizon (H), and branch factor (B). MakSafe yields branch-specific verdicts, deriving safe and unsafe outcomes from the same initial scene, and re-evaluates a scenario after a control update. A single rule check stays well below a millisecond across the reported sweep, and longer horizons slow the TTC check.

title: HyrCap: Hybrid Rank-Calibration of Action Proposals for Temporal Event Understanding
abstract: Temporal action detection in long untrimmed videos suffers from inaccurate localization and low-quality proposals, especially with sparse annotations and ambiguous boundaries. For open-ended video understanding and LLM-driven event analysis, reliable proposals connect temporal localization, event annotation, and semantic understanding. However, conventional temporal action detection (TAD) pipelines lack explicit modeling of proposal localization quality, cross-representation support, and inter-proposal relations. We propose Hybrid Rank-Calibration of Action Proposals (HyrCap), a proposal-centric query-based TAD framework for temporal event understanding. Hybrid combines complementary video features with different localization cues, while Rank-Calibration adjusts proposal ranking confidence to reflect localization reliability and candidate competition. HyrCap treats dense query-based predictions as an over-complete temporal event hypothesis space. Cross-Representation Consensus Calibration, Localization Quality Estimation, and Proposal Redundancy Suppression improve proposal ranking reliability, localization quality, and candidate discrimination. Inspired by LLMs' capabilities in fine-grained semantic recognition, event description, and reasoning, we introduce HyrCap for Semantic Action Understanding, using calibrated proposals for standard TAD and as inputs to LLM-based semantic understanding. We define a staged evaluation protocol to separately measure event localization, segment-level semantic understanding, and combined event understanding performance. Experiments on public benchmarks show that HyrCap achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics and provides a finer-grained paradigm and evaluation protocol for query-based event segmentation and annotation.

title: Online covariance estimation for stochastic gradient descent under Markovian sampling
abstract: We investigate the online overlapping batch-means covariance estimator for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) under Markovian sampling. Under state-dependent Markovian sampling we prove a convergence rate of O(n−(1−2/α0)/8 log n), α0≥16/3 where d is the dimensionality, n denotes observations or SGD iterations, and α0 is a constant related to the mixing properties of the Markov chain. The slower mixing of the state-dependent Markov chain results in a slower rate compared to the i.i.d. case, which we illustrate with a simple example. However, under state-independent Markovian sampling, we obtain the rate O(d n−1/8) matching the best-known convergence rate for independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data. Our analysis overcomes significant challenges arising from Markovian sampling, leading to additional error terms and complex dependencies between the blocks of the batch-means covariance estimator. Moreover, we establish the convergence rate for the first four moments of the l2 norm of the error of SGD dynamics under state-dependent Markovian data, which holds potential interest as an independent result. Numerical illustrations provide confidence intervals for SGD in linear and logistic regression models under Markovian sampling. Additionally, our method is applied to the strategic classification with logistic regression, where adversaries adaptively modify features during training to affect target class classification.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the purchasing decisions of different generations in clothing purchases
abstract: Nakup oblačila se danes pogosto začne, še preden potrošnik zares ve, kaj išče. Med množico izdelkov ga spremljajo priporočila, prilagojene vsebine, virtualni pomočniki in druge rešitve umetne inteligence, ki lahko spletno nakupno pot naredijo bolj osebno in usmerjeno. Vendar na drugi strani zaslona niso vsi potrošniki enaki. Pripadajo različnim generacijam, ki so odraščale v različnih časovnih in tehnoloških okoljih ter s seboj v spletni svet prinašajo svoje nakupne navade, pričakovanja in odnos do novih tehnologij. Diplomsko delo obravnava vpliv umetne inteligence na nakupno odločanje različnih generacij pri spletnem nakupovanju oblačil in nakupovanju oblačil v fizičnih trgovinah. V ospredju so babyboom generacija ter generacije X, Y in Z, pri katerih so obravnavane razlike v nakupnem vedenju, odnosu do umetne inteligence in njenem vplivu na nakupno odločanje. Posebna pozornost je namenjena oblikam umetne inteligence, s katerimi se lahko potrošnik sreča med spletnim nakupovanjem oblačil, ter njihovemu mestu v nakupnem procesu. S povezovanjem sveta mode, spletnega nakupovanja in umetne inteligence delo odpira vprašanje, ali ista tehnologija pri različnih generacijah pomeni tudi enako nakupno izkušnjo. Rezultati raziskave so pokazali, da se generacije razlikujejo predvsem pri prepoznavanju oblik umetne inteligence, pri čemer je najnižjo stopnjo prepoznavanja dosegla generacija Y, ostale generacije so prepoznale vse oblike umetne inteligence, zato je bila hipoteza H1 zavrnjena. Pri zaupanju v umetno inteligenco, njenem vplivu na pogostost nakupovanja pri vseh generacijah, ignoriranju predlogov umetne inteligence pri starejših in poenostavljanju nakupne odločitve rezultati niso potrdili zastavljenih predpostavk, zato so bile hipoteze H2, H3, H4 in H5 zavrnjene.

V ospredju so babyboom generacija ter generacije X, Y in Z, pri katerih so obravnavane razlike v nakupnem vedenju, odnosu do umetne inteligence in njenem vplivu na nakupno odločanje. Posebna pozornost je namenjena oblikam umetne inteligence, s katerimi se lahko potrošnik sreča med spletnim nakupovanjem oblačil, ter njihovemu mestu v nakupnem procesu. S povezovanjem sveta mode, spletnega nakupovanja in umetne inteligence delo odpira vprašanje, ali ista tehnologija pri različnih generacijah pomeni tudi enako nakupno izkušnjo. Rezultati raziskave so pokazali, da se generacije razlikujejo predvsem pri prepoznavanju oblik umetne inteligence, pri čemer je najnižjo stopnjo prepoznavanja dosegla generacija Y, ostale generacije so prepoznale vse oblike umetne inteligence, zato je bila hipoteza H1 zavrnjena. Pri zaupanju v umetno inteligenco, njenem vplivu na pogostost nakupovanja pri vseh generacijah, ignoriranju predlogov umetne inteligence pri starejših in poenostavljanju nakupne odločitve rezultati niso potrdili zastavljenih predpostavk, zato so bile hipoteze H2, H3, H4 in H5 zavrnjene.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Multiple large language models (LLMs) can independently evaluate and select candidate solutions or collaborate to determine which candidates should be selected. However, permanently relying on independent selection may fail to exploit complementary knowledge across models, whereas continuously relying on collaborative selection may introduce unnecessary communication costs, correlated judgments, conformity effects, and additional decision latency. This paper proposes Adaptive Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection (ASCCS), a framework that dynamically switches between these two selection modes according to task characteristics, candidate quality, model disagreement, estimated selection reliability, and computational cost. In self-selection mode, each model independently evaluates available candidates and produces its own selection. In collaborative-selection mode, models exchange candidate assessments, compare evidence, identify disagreements, and jointly determine a selection. A switching controller estimates the expected utility of each mode and selects the mode that best balances decision quality, robustness, latency, and resource consumption. The framework further incorporates confidence calibration, selection-history feedback, disagreement-sensitive collaboration, and an optional abstention mechanism for cases in which neither mode provides sufficient evidence. Unlike a fixed ensemble or an always-collaborative architecture, ASCCS treats the choice of selection mechanism as a dynamic decision problem. This paper formalizes the framework, presents an implementable algorithm, proposes a multi-dimensional evaluation protocol, and identifies research hypotheses for empirical investigation. The framework is designed for candidate-answer selection, reasoning-path selection, tool and model selection, planning, retrieval, and other multi-LLM decision tasks. Its effectiveness remains an empirical question to be established through controlled experiments.

title: Beyond the Black Box: A Semantic Explainable AI Framework for Transparent and Trustworthy E-
authors: Jawale Shivtej Bharat, Prof. S.V. More, Dr. H.B. Jadhav
abstract: Artificial intelligence has become an important part of modern e-commerce, supporting product recommendations, search ranking, customer-review analysis, and personalized shopping experiences. Despite these benefits, customers often receive recommendations without understanding the reasons behind them. This lack of transparency can make it difficult to distinguish a genuinely relevant suggestion from one influenced by popularity, incomplete information, or commercial priorities. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) offers a way to make these decisions more understandable. However, explanations are useful only when they communicate relevant evidence accurately rather than simply presenting convincing language. This paper examines the relationship between XAI, semantic analysis, and transparent decision-making in e-commerce, with particular attention to research trends during 2024, 2025, and 2026. It proposes a conceptual framework that connects customer preferences, product attributes, review sentiment, recommendation models, and evidence-based explanations. The framework is designed to explain why a product may be relevant, which features support the recommendation, and where conflicting information remains. The paper also discusses explanation faithfulness, customer privacy, review reliability, fairness, and the limitations of language-model-generated explanations. Its contribution is a practical design approach for connecting recommendation decisions with verifiable semantic evidence. Future implementation and user testing are required to determine whether this approach improves customer understanding and decision quality in real shopping environments

title: A Dual-Loop Intelligent Teaching Assistant System for Adaptive Web-Based Teaching and Decision Support
abstract: Web-based technologies often fail to fundamentally reshape teaching processes, despite their ubiquity. This study presents a dual-loop intelligent teaching assistant system that integrates natural language processing-driven intent recognition and sentiment analysis within a human-in-the-loop framework. Unlike systems prioritizing pure automation, this study's architecture dynamically routes complex queries to instructors via a visual decision-support dashboard, balancing real-time responsiveness with pedagogical nuance. Empirical results in higher education reveal that while interaction efficiency improved significantly, user satisfaction depended nonlinearly on technical accuracy, heavily influenced by notification strategies and emergent student behaviors, like reverse engineering the bot. These findings underscore the need to evolve web-based tools from static utilities into adaptive sociotechnical ecosystems that actively support both learner autonomy and instructor decision-making.
